section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Utah has the lowest legal BAC limit for drivers in the United States. What is the legal BAC limit for adult drivers (age 21+) in Utah?
note: Utah's legal BAC limit is 0.05% — the lowest of any US state and significantly lower than the 0.08% standard used in all other states. Utah lowered the limit from 0.08% to 0.05% in 2018, making it a leader in impaired driving prevention. This is a critical state-specific fact that is frequently tested on the Utah DMV exam.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At what minimum age can a Utah teenager apply for a learner permit?
options: a:14,b:15,c:15 and a half,d:16
note: Utah allows applicants to apply for a learner permit at age 15. The permit allows supervised driving practice with a licensed driver age 21 or older in the front passenger seat. After holding the permit for 6 months and completing required supervised hours, the teen can apply for a limited-term license.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why is Utah's 0.05% BAC limit significant compared to other states?
options: a:It was set by federal mandate in 2020,b:Utah is the only US state with a 0.05% BAC limit — all other states use 0.08%,c:Utah raised the limit to 0.05% from 0.02% in 2022,d:Utah's 0.05% only applies to commercial drivers
note: Utah is the ONLY US state with a 0.05% BAC limit. Every other state uses 0.08% as the standard per se DUI limit. Utah lowered the limit from 0.08% to 0.05% in 2018 following state legislation. This lower threshold means a person can be legally impaired in Utah at BAC levels that would be legal in other states.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Utah's GDL program, a teen with a learner permit (age 15–16) must complete how many hours of supervised driving before applying for a limited-term license?
options: a:30 hours total,b:40 hours (including 10 at night),c:40 hours (including 10 at night, starting after the first 6 months),d:60 hours total
note: Utah requires learner permit holders to complete 40 hours of supervised driving practice, including at least 10 hours at night, before applying for a limited-term license. The permit must also be held for at least 6 months. These hours must be driven with a licensed adult (21+) in the front seat.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the maximum speed limit on Utah rural interstate highways?
options: a:65 mph,b:70 mph,c:75 mph,d:80 mph
note: Utah allows a maximum speed of 75 mph on rural interstate highways for passenger vehicles. Some sections may have lower posted limits near cities or construction zones. Utah's wide desert highways and open terrain make it one of several western states with higher rural interstate limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Utah's zero tolerance law for drivers under 21 sets the illegal BAC at:
options: a:0.05% — same as the adult limit,b:0.02%,c:0.04%,d:0.00% — any detectable amount
note: Utah has absolute zero tolerance for underage drinking and driving — any detectable amount of alcohol in a driver under 21 is illegal. Combined with Utah's already lower adult BAC limit of 0.05%, Utah has among the strictest DUI laws in the nation. Any BAC reading for a driver under 21 results in DUI charges.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit on Utah urban streets when no speed limit sign is posted?
options: a:20 mph,b:25 mph,c:30 mph,d:35 mph
note: Utah's default urban speed limit is 25 mph when no other limit is posted. In school zones and residential areas, even lower limits may be posted. Always check posted signs — cities like Salt Lake City and Provo have many zones with reduced limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Utah has many canyon roads and mountain passes. When driving downhill on a steep grade, what is the safest technique?
options: a:Apply brakes continuously and steadily throughout the descent,b:Shift to a lower gear before descending to use engine braking, and apply brakes intermittently if needed,c:Increase speed slightly to maintain momentum through curves,d:Turn off the engine to coast down the hill
note: On Utah's steep canyon descents, use engine braking by downshifting before starting the descent. This reduces wear on your brakes and prevents brake fade — a condition where brakes overheat and lose effectiveness. Apply the brakes intermittently in short, firm applications rather than riding them continuously.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Utah, a limited-term license holder (teen age 16–17) has a nighttime driving restriction. When may they NOT drive without a licensed adult?
options: a:Between 10 PM and 6 AM,b:Between 11 PM and 5 AM,c:Between midnight and 5 AM,d:Between midnight and 6 AM
note: Utah limited-term license holders under 17 may not drive between midnight and 6 AM without a licensed adult (21+) in the front seat. This curfew applies from the time the license is issued until the holder turns 17. Exceptions include driving to or from employment, school, or a medical emergency.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a school bus with activated red flashing lights and a stop arm in Utah, you must:
options: a:Stop only if traveling in the same direction as the bus,b:Stop at least 15 feet in all directions on undivided roads until lights stop flashing,c:Slow to 10 mph and pass with caution if no children are crossing,d:Stop only if children are visible outside the bus
note: Utah requires all vehicles on an undivided road to stop at least 15 feet from a school bus with activated red lights, in both directions. Wait until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm retracts before proceeding. On divided highways with a median, only vehicles behind the bus must stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Utah's Move Over law requires drivers approaching a stopped emergency or utility vehicle with flashing lights to:
options: a:Sound their horn as a warning and proceed,b:Only slow down — lane changes are not required,c:Move to a non-adjacent lane if safe, or reduce speed if a lane change is not possible,d:Stop completely until the vehicle departs
note: Utah's Move Over law requires drivers to move to a lane not adjacent to the stopped vehicle if safely possible. If a lane change cannot be made safely, reduce speed to a safe level. Utah's law covers emergency, law enforcement, maintenance, and highway worker vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a diamond-shaped orange sign mean when seen in a work zone?
options: a:A regular warning sign — same as a yellow diamond,b:A construction or work zone warning — heightened attention required,c:A detour sign — follow arrows to alternate route,d:A speed limit change specific to trucks only
note: Orange diamond-shaped signs indicate construction or work zones and require heightened attention. In Utah, fines for traffic violations in work zones are doubled when workers are present. Slow down, watch for workers and equipment, and follow all posted work zone signs and flaggers' directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Utah requires headlights from sunset to sunrise. When else are headlights required in Utah?
options: a:Only during officially declared weather emergencies,b:Whenever windshield wipers are in use due to rain, snow, or fog,c:Anytime outside city limits,d:Only when visibility is reduced to less than 500 feet
note: Utah requires headlights from sunset to sunrise AND whenever weather conditions (rain, snow, fog) require the use of windshield wipers. This rule ensures vehicles are visible to others even when wiper use begins before it is fully dark. If you need your wipers, turn on your headlights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop in Utah, two cars arrive at exactly the same time — one from the north, one from the west. Which car has the right of way?
options: a:The car coming from the north (going south) has the right of way,b:The car coming from the west (going east) has the right of way because it is on the right of the northbound car,c:Both cars must wait for a third vehicle to break the tie,d:The car on the wider road goes first
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at a four-way stop, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The car coming from the west is to the right of the northbound car (from the northbound driver's perspective), so the westbound car has the right of way. The northbound driver yields.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct hand position on the steering wheel recommended by Utah DMV?
options: a:10 o'clock and 2 o'clock,b:9 o'clock and 3 o'clock (or 8 and 4),c:One hand only, at 12 o'clock,d:Any position the driver is comfortable with
note: Utah DMV recommends the 9 and 3 (or 8 and 4) hand position on the steering wheel. This position provides optimal control and reduces risk of injury from an airbag deployment. The older 10 and 2 position is no longer recommended because it puts hands in the path of the deploying airbag.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Utah has high-altitude roads where the air is thinner. How does high altitude affect driving?
options: a:High altitude improves fuel efficiency and braking performance,b:High altitude can reduce engine power and increase stopping distances slightly,c:High altitude has no effect on vehicle performance,d:High altitude reduces tire pressure, requiring constant adjustment
note: Utah's high-altitude roads — some above 10,000 feet — can reduce engine power due to thinner air (less oxygen for combustion). Braking performance is minimally affected, but driver alertness and reaction time can be impaired by altitude sickness. Be especially cautious on mountain passes and canyon roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum following distance recommended in Utah under normal driving conditions?
options: a:1 second,b:2 seconds,c:3 seconds,d:4 seconds
note: Utah recommends a minimum 3-second following distance under normal conditions. On Utah's mountain highways, the 3-second rule should be extended because stopping distances are affected by steep grades and elevation. In snow or ice — common in Utah winters — increase to at least 6–8 seconds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Utah is a semi-arid state with frequent dust storms in desert regions. What should you do if you encounter a sudden dust storm while driving?
options: a:Pull off the road completely, turn off all lights, and remain in the vehicle,b:Pull completely off the road, set the parking brake, turn off lights, and keep your foot off the brake pedal,c:Continue driving at reduced speed with hazard lights on,d:Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights immediately
note: In a sudden dust storm (common in Utah's desert areas), pull as far off the road as possible — ideally into a rest area or parking lot. Turn off all lights (including hazard flashers) and keep your foot off the brake pedal so following drivers cannot mistake your vehicle for a moving car. Remain in the vehicle with seatbelts on. Turning off lights prevents other drivers from following your lights into the stopped vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Utah, can you make a right turn on a red light?
options: a:No — right turns on red are prohibited statewide,b:Yes, after a complete stop and yielding to all traffic and pedestrians, unless a sign prohibits it,c:Yes, without stopping if no traffic is visible,d:Only between 6 AM and 10 PM
note: Right turns on red are permitted in Utah after a complete stop and yielding to all cross traffic and pedestrians. Always check for a 'No Turn on Red' sign first. In Salt Lake City and other urban areas, 'No Turn on Red' signs are common at busier intersections. Always make a complete stop before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Utah uses implied consent laws. A driver suspected of DUI who refuses a chemical test will face:
options: a:No penalty — refusal is a protected right in Utah,b:18-month license revocation and the refusal can be used as evidence,c:A $50 fine only — no license suspension,d:Only a warning for first-time refusals
note: Utah's implied consent law results in an 18-month driver license revocation for a first-offense refusal — longer than many states. The refusal can also be admitted as evidence in court. Given Utah's already strict 0.05% BAC limit, refusing a test rarely helps and typically results in harsher overall consequences.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you NOT use cruise control while driving in Utah?
options: a:Only when driving in school zones,b:On wet, icy, or snow-covered roads; in heavy traffic; on steep mountain grades,c:Only when other passengers are in the vehicle,d:Cruise control is safe on all roads as long as you remain alert
note: Cruise control should not be used in Utah (or anywhere) on wet, icy, or snow-covered roads because it cannot react to sudden changes in traction. On steep mountain grades, cruise control can cause excessive speed on downhills. In heavy traffic, cruise control reduces your ability to quickly respond to sudden stops. Always use cruise control only on open, dry highways.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the blood alcohol concentration for commercial vehicle drivers in Utah?
options: a:0.05% — same as the passenger vehicle limit,b:0.04%,c:0.02%,d:0.00% — zero tolerance
note: Commercial vehicle drivers in Utah are held to a 0.04% BAC limit — lower than Utah's already-strict 0.05% limit for passenger vehicle drivers. This 0.04% limit is federally mandated for CDL holders. Commercial drivers face even stricter standards due to the size and danger of the vehicles they operate.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving in Utah and see a sign that reads 'BEGIN REDUCED SPEED AHEAD.' What does this mean?
options: a:You must reduce speed immediately at the sign,b:A lower speed limit zone begins ahead — reduce speed before reaching it,c:This is an advisory sign only — no legal requirement,d:The speed limit reduces for trucks only
note: A 'REDUCED SPEED AHEAD' sign warns you that a lower speed zone begins ahead. Begin reducing your speed as you approach the new limit sign — do not wait until you reach it. Gradually slow down so you are at the new posted speed when you enter the zone. This sign is commonly used near school zones and construction areas in Utah.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Utah winter driving requires special preparation. Before driving in snow or icy conditions, you should:
options: a:Install snow tires only if driving in the mountains,b:Clear all snow and ice from all windows, lights, and the vehicle roof before driving,c:Only clear the windshield — side windows are not required to be cleared,d:Snow tires are optional — all-season tires are always adequate in Utah
note: Utah requires (and safety demands) clearing ALL snow and ice from your vehicle before driving — including the roof, all windows, lights, and mirrors. Snow left on the roof can slide onto your windshield or fly off and hit other vehicles. Ensure all lights are visible and all windows provide unobstructed sightlines.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, you and another driver arrive at the same time and are facing each other (going in opposite directions). You both intend to go straight. Who goes first?
options: a:The driver on the wider road goes first,b:Either driver may proceed — same-direction conflict, no yield needed if both go straight,c:The driver facing north always has priority,d:The driver with the larger vehicle has priority
note: When two vehicles at a four-way stop are facing each other and both going straight, there is no conflict — you are not crossing each other's path. Both may proceed at roughly the same time. The yield-to-the-right rule only matters when vehicles' paths would cross. If both go straight in opposite directions, no conflict exists.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing on a multi-lane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up and pass in one quick move,b:Rely only on your mirrors to make the lane change,c:Check that the passing lane is clear and signal before changing lanes,d:Always pass on the right regardless of lane markings
note: Before passing on a multi-lane highway, you must first check that the passing lane is clear by using your mirrors and checking blind spots, then signal your intention, and only move over when it is safe. Never rely only on mirrors or pass on the right unless it is legal and safe to do so.

question: Which factor most directly affects braking distance?
options: a:The condition of the pavement.,b:The condition of your brakes and tires.,c:The speed at which your vehicle is traveling.
note: Braking distance is most directly affected by speed: the faster you are going, the much longer it takes to stop, and stopping distance increases more than proportionally with speed. While pavement and brake/tire condition matter, speed is the primary factor that most directly determines how far your vehicle will travel after you begin braking.

question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Drive with your flashers on.,b:Slow down until it passes you.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle using a siren and flashing lights approaches from behind, you must pull over to the right side of the road and stop, if possible, so it can pass safely. Do not stop in an intersection; clear the intersection first, then pull over and wait until the vehicle has passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must signal in which of the following situations?
options: a:When pulling into or out of a parking space.,b:When changing lanes.,c:Any time you are turning or changing lanes (all of the above).
note: You must always signal to let other road users know what you plan to do. Use your turn signal any time you turn, change lanes, or pull into or out of a parking space or the curb. Signaling early and clearly helps prevent crashes by giving others time to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway, you should:
options: a:Get off at the next exit and return safely.,b:Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.,c:Stop and make a U-turn.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, keep going to the next exit, then leave the highway and find a safe way to return. Never stop in a travel lane, back up, or make a U-turn on the interstate, as these actions are extremely dangerous and usually illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, which practice is usually best?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.,b:Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.,c:Accelerate on the ramp to match the speed of freeway traffic and merge safely.
note: On freeway entrance ramps, use the acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches the flow of traffic, then merge when it is safe. Vehicles already on the freeway have the right-of-way, so adjust your speed and gap selection to blend smoothly without forcing others to brake suddenly.

question: You are involved in an accident and another person is injured. What should you do?
options: a:Move the injured away from the scene immediately.,b:Always leave the injured where they are.,c:Not move the injured unnecessarily; keep them warm and provide first aid if qualified.
note: After a crash with injuries, do not move an injured person unless there is immediate danger (such as fire or risk of another collision). Sudden movement can worsen neck, back, or internal injuries. Keep the person warm, reassure them, call 911, and give first aid only if you are trained and it is necessary for life-threatening conditions.

question: How does increasing your vehicle's speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:Increases your field of vision.,b:Makes it easier to see cross traffic.,c:Decreases your field of vision.
note: As your speed increases, your field of vision narrows and you see less to the sides. This “tunnel vision” effect means you have less time to detect hazards, pedestrians, or cross traffic, so you must scan more actively and adjust your speed to conditions.

question: When is it appropriate to honk your horn?
options: a:When passing a bicyclist.,b:When traveling through an intersection.,c:When you see a child who is about to run into the street.
note: Use your horn only to warn others of a potential collision, such as when a child is about to run into the street or another driver is about to hit you. Do not honk routinely at intersections or just to pass; unnecessary horn use can startle others and is often illegal.

question: What should you do first to slow on a slippery surface?
options: a:Engage the parking brake.,b:Firmly apply the brakes.,c:Take your foot off the gas.
note: On slippery roads, sudden braking can cause skids. First, gently ease your foot off the accelerator so the vehicle slows gradually. If you need to slow more, apply the brakes smoothly and gently, and steer carefully to maintain control.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow mean on a traffic signal?
options: a:You may turn immediately without caution.,b:It never appears on real signals.,c:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light — prepare to stop.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turn phase is ending. You should slow down and prepare to stop; complete the turn only if you are already in the intersection and can do so safely before the light turns red.

question: A flashing red signal at an intersection is equivalent to which sign?
options: a:A yield sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A slow sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when it is safe and after yielding to any traffic or pedestrians with the right of way.

question: Only vehicles displaying special plates or placards for persons with disabilities may park in spaces reserved by official sign.
options: a:False,b:True
note: Parking in spaces reserved for persons with disabilities is only allowed for vehicles displaying the proper disability plates or placards issued to a person with a qualifying disability. Others may not use these spaces, even briefly.

question: When is it especially important to slow down?
options: a:Only at night,b:Only when you see a speed limit sign,c:Only during heavy traffic,d:On narrow or winding roads
note: You should slow down on narrow or winding roads because visibility and space to maneuver are limited. It is also important to reduce speed near intersections, pedestrian crossings, and whenever the road is wet, icy, or otherwise hazardous.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Mechanical failures,b:Wildlife on roadways,c:Bad weather,d:Human error by drivers
note: Most crashes result from driver actions such as inattention, speeding, following too closely, or poor decisions, not from mechanical failure or bad weather alone. Safe, attentive driving greatly reduces crash risk.

question: Does drinking coffee after alcohol reduce blood alcohol concentration?
options: a:Yes,b:You yes,c:No
note: Coffee may make you more alert but does not lower blood alcohol concentration or make you sober.

question: When you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle using lights or siren, you must:
options: a:Drive to the right and stop until it passes.,b:Slow down but remain in your lane.,c:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right as safely possible and stopping until it passes. If you are in an intersection, clear the intersection first, then pull over and stop.

question: When driving on wet pavement, remember that:
options: a:Pavement is especially slippery right after it starts to rain.,b:Wet roads cannot cause hydroplaning.,c:You do not need extra space when stopping.
note: When it first starts to rain, water mixes with oil and other residue on the road, making the pavement especially slippery. Slow down, increase following distance, and be alert for hydroplaning on wet roads.

question: If you are involved in a serious motor vehicle crash, what actions should you take?
options: a:Only exchange insurance information and leave immediately,b:Leave the scene and report it later,c:Stop,d:Keep driving to the nearest service station
note: If you are involved in a serious crash, you must stop at once. If possible, move your vehicle out of traffic, check for injuries, call emergency services, and exchange information. You must remain at the scene and report the crash as required by state law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should you complete the turn?
options: a:Into the left lane of the one-way street,b:Into the center of the street,c:Into the right lane of the one-way street,d:Into any lane that looks clear
note: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you should turn into the leftmost lane that is open and safe on the one-way street. Starting and ending in the correct lane helps keep traffic organized and prevents conflicts with other vehicles.

question: If convicted of driving without insurance, how long must you carry SR-22 in Utah?
options: a:Six months.,b:One year.,c:Three years.
note: In Utah, if you are convicted of driving without insurance, you must file an SR‑22 and maintain proof of financial responsibility for three years. This shows the state you are continuously insured during that period before your record is cleared of that requirement.

question: Can large vehicles have blind spots extending far behind them?
options: a:Trucks always have rear sensors that eliminate blind spots,b:True — blind spots can extend up to 200 feet behind large vehicles,c:False — their mirrors cover the rear,d:Only small vehicles have large blind spots
note: Large trucks and buses have very large blind spots directly behind them that can extend up to about 200 feet. If you follow too closely, the driver may not see you at all, and you will have less time to react if the truck stops suddenly. Always leave extra following distance behind large vehicles.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road.,b:Straight ahead at the approaching vehicle.,c:At the vehicle's wheels.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, you should briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road. This reduces glare and helps you avoid being blinded while still keeping your vehicle correctly positioned in your lane.

question: If you borrow an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Ignore minor defects to avoid embarrassment,b:Hide from the owner that you are unfamiliar with the car,c:Assume all vehicles work the same and drive immediately,d:Familiarize yourself with the controls and correct any obvious defects
note: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, take time to learn where the lights, wipers, turn signals, gear selector, parking brake, and other controls are. Also check for and correct any obvious safety defects, such as bad tires or inoperative lights, so you can operate the vehicle safely and legally.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or false: You may pass on a two‑lane roadway when the center line next to your lane is a single solid yellow line.
options: a:True — a single solid yellow always allows passing,b:True — if no oncoming traffic is present,c:Only if the other lane is clear,d:False — you may not pass when the line beside your lane is solid
note: On a two‑lane road, you may not pass if the center line next to your lane is a solid yellow line. A solid yellow line beside your lane means no passing in your direction. Passing is only allowed when the line next to your lane is broken (dashed) and it is otherwise safe to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a stop sign that is not marked by a crosswalk, drivers should stop their vehicles before entering the intersection. True or False?
options: a:False,b:True
note: If there is no stop line or crosswalk at a stop sign, you must stop before entering the intersection. Stop where you can clearly see cross traffic, then yield to any vehicles or pedestrians with the right‑of‑way before proceeding.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:
options: a:Overcorrect to regain control.,b:Steer in the direction of the skid.,c:Turn the wheel into oncoming traffic.
note: When your vehicle begins to skid, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and steer gently in the same direction the rear of the vehicle is sliding. This helps you straighten the vehicle and regain traction without overcorrecting, which can cause a spin.

question: A child must remain in a rear-facing car seat until they are at least what age?
options: a:Three years old,b:Four years old,c:Two years old
note: Children should ride in a rear‑facing car seat until at least age two, and longer if they have not yet reached the seat’s maximum height or weight limit. Rear‑facing seats provide better support for a young child’s head, neck, and spine in a crash.

question: A solid white edge line on the right that slants toward the center of the road indicates:
options: a:You will be required to turn left just ahead.,b:The road will become narrower ahead.,c:There is an intersection just ahead.
note: A solid white edge line marks the right edge of the roadway. When this line angles or slants toward the center of the road, it warns that the road or lane is narrowing ahead, so you should be prepared to adjust your position and speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit indicates:
options: a:The exact speed you must travel to avoid a ticket.,b:The maximum legal speed under ideal road and weather conditions.,c:Only a recommended driving speed.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed allowed under ideal conditions. You may need to drive slower than the posted limit when roads are wet, visibility is poor, traffic is heavy, or other hazards are present.

question: How should you check blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:By turning your head to physically check the blind spot.,b:Only by using the inside rearview mirror.,c:Only by using the outside mirror.
note: Mirrors do not show the entire area around your vehicle. Before changing lanes, you must quickly turn your head to look over your shoulder into the blind spot to be sure no vehicle, motorcycle, or bicycle is hidden beside you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, how should a driver proceed?
options: a:Assume other drivers will yield to you.,b:Maintain speed and proceed as usual.,c:Yield to the vehicle on the right and be prepared to stop to avoid collisions.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), you must slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield to any vehicle already in the intersection and to vehicles on your right. Proceed only when it is safe.

question: You must pull over to the right edge of the road and allow an emergency vehicle to pass:
options: a:Only if it is following you.,b:Only if it is approaching from the opposite direction.,c:When it is using sirens and/or flashing lights, pull to the right and stop when safe, regardless of its direction unless otherwise directed by law enforcement.
note: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle using sirens and flashing lights, you must immediately pull to the right edge of the road and stop, when safe, until it has passed. This applies whether it is coming from behind you or approaching from ahead on a two-way road, unless directed otherwise by a police officer.

question: When you get into a car to drive, what should you adjust first?
options: a:The steering wheel.,b:Your seat.,c:The rearview mirror.
note: Adjust your seat first so you can comfortably reach the pedals, steering wheel, and controls and have a clear view of the road. Once your seating position is correct, adjust mirrors and steering wheel to match that position.

question: Which practice can help conserve gasoline?
options: a:Sitting in your driveway with the car running.,b:Accelerating quickly.,c:Slowing down gradually.
note: To save fuel, avoid rapid acceleration and hard braking. Looking ahead and slowing down gradually lets you maintain smoother speeds, which uses less gasoline than quick starts and stops or unnecessary idling.

question: If an oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane, what should you do?
options: a:Blow your horn and be prepared to brake and steer right,b:You blow your horn,c:It is required to blow your horn
note: If a vehicle is coming toward you in your lane, immediately slow or brake hard, lay on your horn to get the other driver’s attention, and steer to the right side of the road or onto the shoulder if needed. Never swerve left into the oncoming lane, because that greatly increases the risk of a head‑on collision.

question: When a transit vehicle signals to re-enter traffic after stopping, you must:
options: a:Honk to warn it to hurry up.,b:Yield and allow it to merge back safely.,c:Move into the right lane without slowing.
note: When a transit or city bus signals that it is pulling out from a stop, you must yield and allow it to re‑enter traffic when it is safe. Be prepared to slow, change lanes, or stop so the bus can merge smoothly and avoid sudden braking or conflicts with passengers boarding or exiting.

question: On a two-lane road without bike lanes, how should you pass a bicyclist traveling in the same direction?
options: a:Only pass at traffic signals,b:Honk and pass closely to encourage them to move over,c:Pass rapidly without changing lanes,d:Slow down and pass only when you can give at least 3 feet of space
note: On a two‑lane road without bike lanes, treat a bicyclist like a slow‑moving vehicle. Slow down, wait until it is safe, then pass with plenty of clearance—at least 3 feet or more if possible—and only when you can move partially or fully into the oncoming lane without endangering anyone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To change lanes safely you should:
options: a:Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your shoulder,b:Signal only,c:Use turn indicator only
note: To change lanes safely, first signal to let others know your intention, then check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Only move into the new lane when you are sure it is clear and you have enough space.

question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes is considered:
options: a:A good driving habit,b:A bad driving habit,c:Unnecessary and unsafe,d:Only for new drivers
note: Every vehicle has blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Turning your head to quickly check over your shoulder before changing lanes or merging is a critical safety habit that helps you see vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles that might be hidden in your mirrors.

question: Distracted driving is:
options: a:Very uncommon.,b:Extremely risky behavior.,c:Nothing to be concerned about.
note: Distracted driving greatly increases crash risk for drivers, passengers, pedestrians, and other road users.

question: What do regulatory signs do?
options: a:Indicate nearby services,b:Warn of hazardous conditions,c:Serve as tourist information,d:Indicate what drivers must or must not do
note: Regulatory signs tell drivers the laws and rules for the area (e.g., speed limits, no turns, lane use restrictions) and are enforceable.

question: What does a green arrow signal mean?
options: a:A green arrow is only used on one-way streets,b:A green arrow allows you to go straight regardless of arrows,c:A green arrow is the same as a circular green for all movements,d:Traffic indicated by the arrow may proceed and must turn in the direction shown
note: A green arrow permits traffic in the indicated lane to proceed in the arrow’s direction; it controls that turn specifically.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does an advisory speed sign (speed restriction sign) typically indicate?
options: a:The maximum legal speed for the roadway.,b:The recommended safe speed for a specific area such as a curve or turn.,c:The speed drivers should use in heavy traffic.
note: Advisory speed signs provide a recommended speed for curves and other conditions; they are not necessarily the posted maximum but indicate safe speed for that feature.

question: Motorcycles are entitled to:
options: a:The bicycle lane.,b:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,c:Half the width of a lane.
note: Motorcycles are considered motor vehicles and are entitled to the full width of a traffic lane, just like cars and trucks. Other drivers should not crowd or share a lane side‑by‑side with a motorcycle, because they need the entire lane for safe maneuvering and to avoid road hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You want to turn left at an intersection; the light is green but oncoming traffic is heavy. What should you do?
options: a:Use the next intersection to turn.,b:Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.,c:Wait in the intersection and complete your left turn when it is safe to do so.
note: With a green light and heavy oncoming traffic, you may pull into the intersection, keeping the crosswalk clear, and wait with your wheels straight. When there is a safe gap or the light turns yellow/red and oncoming traffic stops, complete your left turn.

question: When driving through an area where children are playing, you should expect them to:
options: a:Know when it is safe to cross the street.,b:Stop at the curb before crossing the street.,c:Run out into the street without looking.
note: Children often do not judge traffic well and may suddenly run into the street without looking. In areas where children are playing, slow down, cover the brake, and be prepared to stop quickly.

question: Why must you be especially alert for motorcycles?
options: a:They rarely use headlights.,b:Motorcyclists are less skilled than other drivers.,c:They are smaller and harder to see than cars.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and can be hidden easily in blind spots or behind other vehicles. Because they are harder to see and their speed and distance can be difficult to judge, you must look carefully and check mirrors and blind spots before turning or changing lanes.

question: As you approach an accident scene, what should you generally do?
options: a:Stop and gather around to watch the scene,b:Pull off and block traffic so emergency responders can access the area,c:Drive by slowly and record the incident on your phone,d:Keep your attention on driving and keep moving unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived
note: At an accident scene, keep your attention on the road, reduce speed if needed, and continue driving unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived and you can safely assist. Do not stop to watch, take photos, or block access for emergency vehicles.

question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching?
options: a:Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.,b:Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.,c:See if you can reach your destination before it catches you.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as possible and stopping until it has passed, unless directed otherwise. If you are in an intersection, clear the intersection first, then pull over and stop.

question: Which actions can reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Ignore other drivers' behavior entirely.,b:Only obey posted speed limits.,c:Allow extra travel time and use proper signals.
note: Allowing extra travel time, using proper signals, and following traffic rules helps you stay calm and predictable. This reduces frustration for you and others, which lowers the chance of road rage or aggressive driving incidents.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes you should:
options: a:Glance over your shoulder to check blind spots, use your mirrors, and signal in advance.,b:Signal at least 500 feet before your lane change in residential areas.,c:Rely solely on your mirrors.
note: When changing lanes, always check your mirrors, then quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot, and signal well in advance—typically at least 100 feet in city/residential areas and 300 feet or more at higher speeds. Never rely only on mirrors, because vehicles can be hidden in blind spots.

question: If your wheels slip off the road edge, you should:
options: a:Jerk the wheel to re-enter immediately.,b:Slow down gradually and steer back onto the pavement when safe.,c:Speed up and re-enter quickly.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, keep a firm grip on the wheel, ease off the accelerator, and slow down gradually. Once the car is under control and there is a clear gap in traffic, gently steer back onto the pavement. Avoid jerking the wheel or speeding up, which can cause you to lose control.

question: When changing lanes, which should you NOT do?
options: a:Give a turn signal to indicate your intent.,b:Fail to check side and rearview mirrors.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: Before changing lanes, you should always check your mirrors, look over your shoulder for blind spots, and signal your intention. Failing to check your mirrors is unsafe because you may not see vehicles approaching from behind or already in the lane you want to enter.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to signal every time you pull away from a curb.
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must signal any time you pull away from a curb so other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know you are about to enter the traffic lane. Signaling clearly and early helps prevent collisions and lets others adjust their speed or position.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing you should:
options: a:Ignore it if no train is visible.,b:Speed up to cross quickly.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: When you approach a railroad crossing, you should slow down, look and listen for trains, and be ready to stop. If warning lights are flashing, gates are down, or a train is clearly approaching, you must stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail and remain stopped until it is safe to proceed.

question: It is unlawful for a car to share a single lane with a motorcycle.
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: A motorcycle is entitled to use a full traffic lane, and a driver of a car must not try to share the same single lane side‑by‑side with a motorcycle. This gives the motorcyclist enough space to maneuver and avoid hazards.

question: If your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement, what is the proper reaction?
options: a:Take your foot off the accelerator, steer parallel to the road, slow down, then gently steer back onto the pavement when safe.,b:Accelerate and steer back onto the road quickly.,c:Stop immediately on the shoulder.
note: If your right wheels leave the pavement, stay calm and keep a firm grip on the wheel. Ease off the accelerator, keep your wheels parallel to the roadway, and slow down gradually. When the car is under control and traffic is clear, gently steer back onto the pavement without jerking the wheel.

question: Which of these may cause distracted driving?
options: a:Only eating,b:Only talking on the phone,c:Any activity that takes your attention away from driving,d:Only using navigation systems
note: Distracted driving is caused by any activity that takes your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving. Examples include eating, using a phone, adjusting navigation or music systems, and talking to passengers. You should minimize all such distractions while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving in the left lane and want to move into the right lane. What should you do?
options: a:Check mirrors, signal, and glance over your right shoulder before moving right.,b:Look only in your mirrors and move over if you don’t see a vehicle.,c:Check only the rearview mirror before changing lanes.
note: Before moving from the left lane into the right lane, you must check your mirrors, signal, and then quickly glance over your right shoulder to check your blind spot. Only change lanes when you are sure the lane is clear and you can move over safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road you must:
options: a:Flash your lights at oncoming traffic to warn them.,b:Use the shoulder to pass.,c:Move into the oncoming traffic lane and complete the pass safely.
note: On a two-lane, two-way road, you may pass a slower vehicle only by moving fully into the oncoming traffic lane when passing is permitted and it is safe. You must have enough clear distance ahead, obey any no-passing markings or signs, and return to your lane as soon as it is safe. You may not use the shoulder or rely on flashing lights to oncoming traffic.

question: Which technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Reduce your speed and increase following distance.,b:Add extra weight to improve traction.,c:Get off the highways as quickly as possible.
note: On icy or snowy roads, the most important safety technique is to slow down and increase your following distance. Reduced speed gives you more time to react, and extra space allows for the much longer stopping distances needed on slippery surfaces. Extra weight or leaving the highway are not general safety requirements; careful speed and space management are.

question: A diamond-shaped sign serves as a:
options: a:Road hazard/warning sign.,b:School crossing sign (typically pentagon-shaped, not diamond).,c:Interstate route sign.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are standard warning signs. They alert drivers to hazards or changes in road conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings. While some school-related warnings may use a diamond shape, the specific school crossing sign is typically a pentagon (five-sided) shape, not a diamond. Interstate route signs are shield-shaped.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as a vehicle to your right. You should:
options: a:Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.,b:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.,c:Speed up and get through the intersection.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, if you and another vehicle arrive at the same time, you must yield to the vehicle on your right. Slowing down and allowing the vehicle on your right to go first reduces the risk of collision and follows right-of-way rules. Never speed up or force another driver to stop in this situation.

question: Should you use high beams when driving in fog?
options: a:True,b:False
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams, combined with reduced speed, help you see the road and be seen by others more effectively in foggy conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left, what should you do?
options: a:Signal, move into the left lane if applicable, slow gradually, and watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians,b:Stop in the middle of the intersection to wait for a gap,c:Turn without signaling to avoid confusing other drivers,d:Accelerate briefly and then turn quickly
note: Before a left turn, signal well in advance, move into the correct left lane if there is one, slow smoothly, and scan for oncoming traffic, pedestrians, and cyclists. Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians in the crosswalk, and only turn when the path is clear and safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is correct?
options: a:Speeding increases both the risk and severity of crashes.,b:Driving too slowly on some highways can be hazardous.,c:Speeding is safe if you are an experienced driver.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic on some roads can be dangerous because it may cause other drivers to brake suddenly or make risky passing maneuvers. Safe driving means choosing a speed that is legal and appropriate for conditions—not too fast and not unreasonably slow.

question: Which factor does NOT affect vehicle stopping distance?
options: a:Your reaction time.,b:The condition of your brakes.,c:The time of day.,d:Your vehicle’s speed.
note: Stopping distance is made up of your reaction distance and your braking distance. It is affected by how quickly you react, the condition of your brakes and tires, your speed, and the road surface. The time of day by itself does not directly change how far it takes your vehicle to stop.

question: When passing a large vehicle, what should a small vehicle driver be prepared for?
options: a:Loud noises only.,b:Wind gusts produced by the large vehicle.,c:Increased air pollution.
note: When you pass a large truck or bus, the air it pushes aside can create strong wind gusts that may pull or push your vehicle. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to make small steering corrections to stay in your lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at an open (uncontrolled) intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:One driver may continue without stopping.,b:The driver on the left.,c:The driver on the right.
note: At an open (uncontrolled) intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals.

question: If you notice a defect that could affect your vehicle’s safe operation, what should you do?
options: a:Drive more slowly and postpone repairs,b:Only repair it if it fails during a trip,c:Wait until you can afford the repair,d:Correct the defect as soon as possible before driving
note: Any defect that could affect safe operation—such as problems with brakes, steering, tires, or lights—must be repaired before driving. Continuing to drive, even more slowly, can still be dangerous because the defect may cause you to lose control or be unable to avoid a crash.

question: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving:
options: a:Do not affect driving abilities.,b:Help maintain driver alertness.,c:Are distracting activities.
note: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is a distraction because it takes at least one hand off the wheel and can draw your eyes and attention away from the road. Any activity that diverts your focus from driving increases your risk of a collision.

question: Is it lawful to drive at night using only your parking lights?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Parking lights alone are not bright enough for safe night driving and do not meet legal requirements. At night or in low visibility, you must use your headlights so you can see the road ahead and so other drivers can see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in a residential area?
options: a:20 mph.,b:15 mph.,c:25 mph.
note: In most U.S. states, the default speed limit in residential or business districts is 25 mph unless signs show a different limit. This lower speed gives you more time to react to pedestrians, children, and vehicles entering from driveways or side streets.

question: “Highway hypnosis” can result from:
options: a:Too much sleep the night before a trip.,b:Frequent rest stops.,c:Staring at the roadway for long periods.
note: Highway hypnosis is a drowsy, trance-like state that can occur when you stare straight ahead at the road for long periods without actively scanning. To prevent it, move your eyes regularly, take breaks, and stop to rest if you feel tired.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who must you yield to?
options: a:Drivers who arrived before you.,b:Drivers who arrived after you.,c:Drivers on your left only.
note: At a four‑way stop, you must first yield to any drivers who arrived at the intersection before you. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. After yielding as required, each driver proceeds in the order of arrival.

question: Why is it important to maintain a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:It prevents distractions from other vehicles.,b:It keeps traffic flowing at a steady pace.,c:It gives you time to react to unexpected actions by other road users.
note: Maintaining a space cushion gives you room and time to react if another driver brakes suddenly, changes lanes, or makes a mistake. Extra space reduces the chance of rear‑end collisions and allows you to slow, stop, or steer away from danger more safely.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Never pass them.,b:Avoid driving alongside them and do not tailgate.,c:Flash your lights at them to get their attention.
note: Trucks and buses have large blind spots along both sides and directly behind them. To stay visible, avoid driving right alongside these vehicles and never follow too closely. Pass promptly and safely, and leave extra space so the driver can see you in their mirrors.

question: If a vehicle comes toward you with high beams on and blinding headlights, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to pass quickly,b:Flash your high beams back to warn them,c:Keep looking at the lights to maintain lane position,d:Look away from the headlights toward the right edge of the road until the vehicle passes
note: When an oncoming vehicle’s high beams are blinding, do not look directly at the lights. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use the road’s edge line as a guide until the vehicle passes. This helps preserve your night vision and keeps you in your lane.

question: When approaching a flashing red traffic signal, a driver must:
options: a:Slow down at the light.,b:Merge to the right.,c:Stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when safe.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield the right‑of‑way as needed, and then proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: When driving in fog, you should use your low beam headlights:
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Use low beam headlights in fog because their light aims down toward the road and reduces glare. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

question: A learner's permit allows practice driving while supervised by whom?
options: a:A licensed driver education teacher only.,b:An approved driving instructor,c:Any licensed driver.
note: With a learner’s permit, you must be supervised by a properly licensed driver who meets your state’s age and license requirements, often a parent, guardian, or other responsible adult. It is not limited only to professional or approved driving instructors; any qualifying licensed driver may supervise, as specified by state law.

question: If there is an oncoming car on your left and a bicyclist on your right, what should you do?
options: a:Pull onto the shoulder between them,b:Try to split the space between them,c:Pass the bicyclist immediately and hope the oncoming car yields,d:Let the oncoming car pass first
note: When facing hazards on both sides, deal with them one at a time. Slow down and let the oncoming car pass first, keeping a safe space cushion. After the oncoming vehicle has gone by and the lane is clear, you can move slightly away from the bicyclist and pass only when it is safe.

question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Your body weight.,b:How much time passes between drinks.,c:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.
note: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is determined mainly by how much alcohol you consume, your body weight, and how quickly your body can process the alcohol (time between drinks). The type or flavor of alcoholic beverage does not change how your body absorbs alcohol—only the total amount of alcohol matters.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is an allowable passing situation?
options: a:Passing by using the highway shoulder,b:Passing in a curve or on a hill because you think no vehicle is coming,c:Passing when your lane is next to a solid yellow line,d:Passing when the center line next to your lane is a broken yellow line and the passing lane is clear
note: You may pass another vehicle only when the center line next to your lane is a broken yellow line and you have enough clear distance ahead. You must never pass on the shoulder or when your side of the center line is solid, and you should not pass on hills or curves where you cannot see oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a street that has multiple lanes going in your direction, you should:
options: a:Turn into the lane closest to your original lane.,b:Turn into the middle lane.,c:Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.
note: When you turn onto a multi‑lane street, you must enter the lane that is closest to the lane you turned from. For example, if you turn left from the leftmost lane, you must enter the leftmost lane of the new road. After you complete the turn and it is safe, you can change lanes if needed.

question: Signs that warn drivers about hazardous conditions ahead are called:
options: a:Guide signs,b:Warning signs,c:Information signs,d:Regulatory signs
note: Warning signs are usually yellow and black and are used to alert drivers to hazards or changes in road conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or merging traffic, so drivers can adjust speed and position in advance.

question: At a railroad crossing that has no flashing lights or gates, you should slow down, look, and listen.
options: a:True,b:False
note: At railroad crossings without flashing lights or gates, you must slow down, look carefully in both directions, and listen for trains before crossing. Be prepared to stop if a train is approaching, and never proceed unless you are sure the tracks are clear.

question: What is a safe way to drive through a curve?
options: a:Slow down entering and accelerate gradually exiting.,b:Maintain constant speed throughout.,c:Speed up entering and slow down exiting.
note: Before entering a curve, reduce your speed so you can steer smoothly and stay in your lane. As you pass the midpoint and see the road straightening, you can gradually accelerate again. Entering too fast makes it harder to control the vehicle and stay on your intended path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to exceed the posted speed limit when passing another vehicle?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must never drive faster than the posted speed limit, even when passing another vehicle. When passing, you should use a passing zone, signal, and complete the maneuver within the speed limit and available distance, returning to your lane only when it is safe.

question: What should you do to avoid collisions caused by vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Rely solely on blind spot detection systems,b:Adjust your mirrors every five minutes while driving,c:Quickly turn your head and glance over your shoulder to check before changing lanes,d:Honk before changing lanes to warn other motorists
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see with your mirrors alone. Before changing lanes, you should quickly turn your head and glance over your shoulder to check these areas. Relying only on mirrors or technology can miss vehicles riding in your blind spots.

question: Are drivers always required to stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road?
options: a:True — but only during school hours,b:False — only drivers behind the bus must stop,c:False — only if children are present,d:True — drivers in both directions must stop for a stopped school bus with flashing red lights on a two-lane road
note: On a two-lane road with no physical divider, drivers in both directions must stop when a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended. You must remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the bus moves or the driver signals you to proceed.

question: If you begin to feel sleepy while driving, the best action is to:
options: a:Open your window.,b:Get some coffee.,c:Stop driving and rest.
note: Driving while fatigued is dangerous; the safest option is to stop driving and rest or switch drivers.

question: Is a railroad crossbuck sign treated the same as a yield sign?
options: a:False,b:True
note: A railroad crossbuck sign means you must yield to trains. Slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. If a train is approaching, you must stop and wait; trains always have the right-of-way at crossings.

question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what must you do when turning?
options: a:You retain exclusive right-of-way to turn without yielding.,b:You may no longer turn; proceed only straight.,c:Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.
note: A green arrow gives you a protected turn, but when it changes to a solid green light you must treat the turn as unprotected. You may still turn, but you must first yield to oncoming traffic and any pedestrians in the crosswalk, then turn when it is safe.

question: Which of the following about seat belts and child restraints is correct?
options: a:An airbag can be dangerous to an infant or small child.,b:You should never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with an active airbag.,c:Always ensure all passengers are using seat belts or appropriate child restraints (best single guidance).
note: The safest and most complete guidance is to make sure every occupant uses the correct restraint: adults in seat belts and children in properly sized child seats or booster seats. Airbags can seriously injure infants and small children, so they should never ride in front of an active airbag, but the primary rule for drivers is to ensure that everyone is correctly restrained every trip.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When entering a highway where other cars are present.,b:When anything makes driving conditions less than ideal.,c:When you see a police car.
note: You must slow below the posted speed limit whenever conditions are less than ideal, such as rain, snow, ice, fog, heavy traffic, or poor visibility. The law requires you to drive at a speed that is safe for current conditions, and you can be cited for driving too fast for conditions even if you are under the posted limit.

question: If a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing on a private road, must you stop?
options: a:False,b:True
note: School‑bus stopping laws generally apply on public roads. On private property such as private roads, parking lots, or driveways, the specific public‑road school‑bus statutes usually do not apply in the same way. You should still use extreme caution and be prepared to stop for children, but the legal requirement to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights is typically written for public roadways.

question: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane (skid on water), should you immediately apply the brakes?
options: a:No — you should release the accelerator and steer to regain control,b:Yes — apply the brakes quickly,c:Yes — pump the brakes rapidly,d:Yes — shift into neutral and keep accelerating
note: When your vehicle hydroplanes, the tires lose contact with the road and you have very little traction. Slamming on the brakes can cause a complete loss of control. Instead, ease off the accelerator, keep the steering wheel straight or make only gentle corrections, and allow the vehicle to slow down gradually until the tires regain contact with the road.

question: If you must stop along the road at night, what should you do?
options: a:Turn off all lights,b:Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low-beam headlights on,c:Use only your parking lights,d:Use high beams to warn other drivers
note: If you must stop along the road at night, you want other drivers to see you clearly without being blinded. Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low‑beam headlights on so your vehicle is visible from a distance. Avoid using only parking lights or high beams, which either don’t provide enough warning or can glare into other drivers’ eyes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should:
options: a:Force their way into traffic.,b:Assume they have the right-of-way.,c:Yield to traffic already on the public road.
note: When entering a public road from a driveway or private road, you must yield to all traffic already on the roadway. Wait until there is a safe gap and then merge; you do not have the right-of-way in this situation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should drivers do when approaching a steady red traffic light?
options: a:Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.,b:Come to a complete stop; right turns may be allowed unless prohibited.,c:Continue driving because they have the right-of-way.
note: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or stop line. After stopping, you may turn right (and sometimes left from a one-way to a one-way) only if there is no sign prohibiting it and after yielding to pedestrians and other traffic.

question: A leaking exhaust system can:
options: a:Cause excessive oil use.,b:Require your vehicle to have a tune-up sooner than normal.,c:Make you drowsy while driving because of fumes.
note: A leaking exhaust system can let carbon monoxide and other fumes enter the passenger compartment. Breathing these fumes can make you drowsy, impair your driving, and in high concentrations can cause carbon monoxide poisoning or death. Any suspected exhaust leak should be repaired immediately.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a steady green light, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and any other traffic with the right-of-way,b:Always come to a complete stop before turning,c:Honk to warn pedestrians,d:Turn without yielding if you think the way is clear
note: A green light allows you to turn right if it is safe, but you must first yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any oncoming or cross traffic that has the right-of-way. Do not turn until the path is clear and it is safe to complete the turn.

question: What shape is a stop sign?
options: a:A rectangle,b:A diamond,c:An octagon,d:A circle
note: A stop sign is an octagon, which has eight sides. This unique shape helps drivers recognize it quickly, even in poor visibility, and indicates that they must come to a complete stop at the sign.

question: If another vehicle may hit you, what should you do first?
options: a:Wave your arms to attract attention.,b:Turn on your emergency lights only.,c:Sound your horn to warn the other driver.
note: Sounding your horn is the correct first action when you believe another vehicle may hit you. The horn is designed to quickly alert other road users to your presence and potential danger, often giving them just enough time to react and avoid a collision.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked on the side of the road, you should:
options: a:Speed up to pass quickly.,b:Assume the driver might open a door and proceed cautiously.,c:Slam on your brakes as you pass.
note: When passing a parked vehicle, you should always assume someone might open a door or pull out suddenly. Slow slightly if needed, leave extra space, and be prepared to brake. This cautious approach helps you avoid dooring crashes and sudden movements from the parked vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To enter a freeway you should:
options: a:Signal, yield to existing traffic, and enter at the same speed as traffic.,b:Signal and enter the freeway; freeway traffic must yield.,c:Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
note: When entering a freeway, use the on‑ramp and acceleration lane to build up speed, signal, and merge at or near the speed of traffic. You must yield to vehicles already on the freeway and only move over when there is a safe gap.

question: What is the most important rule about speed management when driving through curves?
options: a:Drive at the posted limit through the entire curve and slow at the sharpest part.,b:Accelerate gently before you enter the curve.,c:Slow down before you enter the curve.
note: Before a curve, you should slow down to a safe speed while your vehicle is still traveling straight. Braking in the curve can cause loss of traction because your tires are already working to turn. Enter the curve at a safe speed, then maintain or gently accelerate through it to keep good control.

question: Which of the following is hardest to see at night?
options: a:Pavement markings,b:Other vehicles,c:Road signs,d:Pedestrians
note: Pedestrians are usually the hardest to see at night because they are smaller, often not illuminated, and may wear dark clothing. Unlike signs and lane markings, which are typically reflective, pedestrians can blend into the background, so you must scan carefully and reduce speed where people may be walking.

question: When stopped on an uphill slope you should:
options: a:Reduce following distance normally.,b:Always apply the parking brake only.,c:Allow a larger space cushion in front of you.
note: On an uphill, leave extra space in front of you so that if the vehicle ahead rolls backward when starting, it will not hit you. This larger space cushion gives you time to react and helps prevent rear-end collisions on slopes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection from different highways simultaneously, who yields?
options: a:The vehicle on the right yields to the left.,b:Either vehicle may proceed.,c:The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right‑of‑way rule helps keep traffic movement predictable and reduces the chance of collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot when you are:
options: a:Pulling toward or away from a curb.,b:Changing lanes.,c:Turning left or right.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see with your mirrors alone. You must quickly look over your shoulder to check these areas whenever you change lanes or move toward or away from a curb, because a vehicle, bicyclist, or motorcycle could be hidden there. When turning left or right at low speed from a stopped position, you mainly rely on turning your head and mirrors to scan the intersection, but the classic blind‑spot check is especially critical for lane changes and lateral movements along the roadway.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, you should:
options: a:Honk your horn and turn off the ignition immediately.,b:Turn on hazards and brace yourself without slowing.,c:Work harder to steer.
note: If power steering fails, the steering wheel will become much harder to turn, but you can still steer the vehicle. Firmly grip the wheel, steer with extra effort, and gradually slow down by easing off the accelerator. When it is safe, signal and move to the side of the road, then stop and get the problem checked before driving again.

question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:
options: a:A serious traffic safety problem.,b:Safe if you have only had a few drinks.,c:A minor traffic safety problem.
note: Any amount of drinking can impair your judgment, reaction time, and coordination. Driving after drinking is a major traffic safety problem and greatly increases your risk of a crash, arrest, injury, or death for you and others on the road.

question: Which action helps prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Before stopping, signal your intentions early.,b:Avoid sudden stops whenever possible.,c:Release the gas pedal to begin slowing, then apply the brakes smoothly and steadily.
note: To help prevent rear-end collisions, start slowing early and smoothly. First ease off the accelerator so your vehicle begins to slow, then apply steady, firm pressure to the brakes. This gives drivers behind you more time to see that you are slowing and react safely, instead of being surprised by a sudden stop.

question: On a road without sidewalks, which way should a pedestrian walk?
options: a:On the same side as the direction traffic is moving.,b:On the side with the lightest traffic.,c:Facing oncoming traffic (on the side facing traffic).
note: On roads without sidewalks, pedestrians should walk facing oncoming traffic. Walking on the side of the road where vehicles are coming toward you lets you see approaching cars and gives you more time to react if a driver drifts toward the edge of the road.

question: A yellow traffic signal that flashes on and off means:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A flashing yellow traffic signal means you must slow down and proceed with caution. You do not need to stop unless necessary for safety, but you must be prepared to yield and watch carefully for other vehicles, pedestrians, or hazards in the intersection.

question: Drivers should recognize that large trucks:
options: a:Do not need more room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.,b:Can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:Have large blind spots.
note: Large trucks have much bigger blind spots than passenger cars, especially directly behind them and along both sides near the cab and trailer. If you cannot see the truck driver’s mirrors, the driver probably cannot see you. Avoid lingering in these no-zones and give trucks extra space to turn, change lanes, and stop.

question: At dusk or on overcast days you should:
options: a:Turn on your headlights and use low beams when appropriate.,b:Drive using your four-way flashers.,c:Drive using only your parking lights.
note: At dusk, dawn, and on overcast days, turn on your headlights so others can see you more easily, even if you can still see the road. Use low beams when there is oncoming traffic or when you are following another vehicle so you do not blind other drivers.

question: Why exercise extra caution near a pedestrian using a white cane?
options: a:They are necessarily deaf.,b:They are law enforcement personnel.,c:They are blind or visually impaired and may not see you.
note: A white cane indicates the pedestrian is blind or visually impaired. They may not see you and may rely on sound to judge traffic, so you must yield and use extra caution. Do not assume they are deaf; the cane only indicates visual impairment.

question: When you approach a railroad crossing with flashing signals, you should:
options: a:Stop at least 15 feet from the tracks and look for a train.,b:Slow down and look for a train.,c:Proceed if you do not see a train.
note: Flashing lights at a railroad crossing mean a train is approaching. You must stop at least 15 feet from the tracks, look and listen for trains, and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and it is safe to proceed.

question: A motorist making a left turn must yield to a bicyclist entering the intersection from the opposite direction. True or False?
options: a:True,b:False
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic, including bicyclists. Treat a bicycle like any other vehicle in the oncoming lane and wait for the bicyclist to clear the intersection before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver behind you wants to pass, how should you respond?
options: a:Drive at the same speed as before.,b:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,c:Slow down to give the other driver space to pass easily.
note: If another driver wants to pass you, maintain a steady speed or slightly slow down to create more space ahead of you. This gives the passing driver more room to move back into the lane safely and reduces the risk of a collision.

question: Signs indicating areas of public recreation and cultural interest are what color?
options: a:Brown.,b:Red.,c:Green.
note: Brown traffic signs are used for recreational, cultural, and historical interest areas. They help drivers find parks, campgrounds, historic sites, and similar destinations.

question: When riding in a vehicle, how should small children be secured?
options: a:Never allow a child to ride unless properly fastened into an appropriate child safety seat.,b:They will be safe if they are standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.,c:They may be safely held by a strong adult.
note: Small children must always be secured in an appropriate, properly installed child safety seat or approved child restraint system. Standing on the floor or being held by an adult is extremely dangerous; in a crash, the forces are far too strong for anyone to hold a child safely. Using the correct child seat greatly reduces the risk of serious injury.

question: Which traffic light indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution?
options: a:A steady yellow light,b:A steady green light,c:A flashing yellow light,d:A flashing red light
note: A flashing yellow signal warns drivers to slow down, proceed with caution, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: Which statement about drowsy drivers is correct?
options: a:Opening a window or turning up the radio will reliably keep them alert,b:Drinking coffee permanently cures drowsiness while driving,c:Drowsy drivers can perform so poorly that they may appear to be intoxicated,d:Drowsiness only affects unskilled drivers
note: Drowsiness impairs judgment and reaction time; it can make driving performance similar to that of drunk drivers. Temporary measures rarely work.

question: Are you permitted to drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is being lowered or raised?
