options: a:Yes,b:Yes, but only if you do not see a train coming.,c:No — never drive around or under a lowering or raising gate.
note: You must never drive around, under, or through a railroad crossing gate while it is lowering, down, or rising. Flashing lights, bells, and gates mean a train is approaching or nearby, and trains cannot stop quickly. Always wait until the lights stop flashing, the gates are fully raised, and the tracks are clear before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before moving from the right lane into the left lane on a multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Check your mirrors and turn on your signal, but you do not need to look over your shoulder.,b:Check your mirrors, turn on your signal, and look over your left shoulder for vehicles in your blind spot before changing lanes.,c:Look only in your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
note: Before changing lanes, you should check your mirrors, look over your shoulder toward the lane you want to enter to check your blind spot, signal, and then move when it is safe. Mirrors alone do not show vehicles in your blind spots, so a quick head check is essential to avoid colliding with a vehicle you cannot see in your mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers may not pass from either side of which centerline?
options: a:Combination solid and broken yellow.,b:Single broken yellow.,c:Double solid yellow.
note: A double solid yellow centerline means traffic in both directions is prohibited from passing. You may cross it only when turning left into or out of a driveway or side road where it is safe and legal, but you may not use the opposing lane to pass another vehicle.

question: What does a driver's left arm extended upward indicate?
options: a:They intend to turn right.,b:They intend to turn left.,c:They intend to stop.
note: Standard hand signals: left arm straight out indicates a left turn, left arm extended upward indicates a right turn, and left arm extended downward indicates slowing or stopping. These signals are used when turn signals are not working or are hard to see.

question: Work zones may be which of the following?
options: a:Never require drivers to slow down or use extra caution.,b:Always stationary and marked with black and white signs.,c:Marked with orange signs and may be moving or stationary.
note: Work zones are usually marked with orange signs and may be either stationary (like a fixed construction area) or moving (such as a line-painting or maintenance vehicle). Drivers must slow down, obey posted work-zone speed limits, and use extra caution around workers and equipment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your slow driving causes traffic to back up on a two-lane, two-way road, what should you do?
options: a:Keep driving at the same speed.,b:Pull off the road to let traffic pass.,c:Speed up to restore traffic flow.
note: On a two-lane, two-way road, if your slow speed is causing a line of vehicles to form behind you, you should safely pull off the road or into a turnout where allowed and let the traffic pass. This helps prevent unsafe passing and reduces the risk of rear-end or head-on collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, what is the correct action?
options: a:Make a last-second turn from your lane,b:Stop and reverse back to the exit,c:Continue to the next exit or safe turnaround and do not back up on the shoulder,d:Cross the median to return to the exit
note: If you miss your freeway exit, stay calm and continue to the next exit or another safe place to turn around. Never stop, back up on the freeway or shoulder, or cross the median, as these actions are extremely dangerous and illegal in most jurisdictions.

question: Which describes a good defensive driver?
options: a:Drives slowly at all times.,b:Looks ahead for the actions of other drivers and anticipates problems.,c:Travels at a constant speed regardless of conditions.
note: A good defensive driver looks well ahead, watches what other road users are doing, and anticipates potential hazards. They adjust speed and position to conditions instead of driving slowly all the time or keeping a constant speed regardless of traffic, weather, or road conditions.

question: Your vehicle's brake lights tell other drivers that you are:
options: a:Slowing down or stopping.,b:Changing lanes.,c:Making a turn.
note: Brake lights warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down or stopping so they can react in time and avoid a rear‑end collision. They do not indicate lane changes or turns; those are signaled with your turn signals.

question: How should drivers react to a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Treat it like a stop sign: come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe,b:Drive through if no crossing traffic is present,c:Only stop if a police officer is nearby,d:Slow down and proceed without stopping
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: Should you avoid driving alongside large vehicles for long periods?
options: a:True — avoid lingering beside large vehicles because of their blind spots,b:False — large vehicles have small blind spots,c:False — it is safer to stay beside them,d:True — because they always drive slower
note: Large trucks and buses have large blind spots along both sides, especially on the right. Avoid driving next to them for long periods; either pass promptly and safely or drop back so the driver can see you.

question: Should drivers continually work to improve driving and observation skills?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Driving always involves changing conditions and potential hazards, so continually improving your observation and driving skills helps you spot risks earlier and respond more safely.

question: What color are signs that tell the distance to the next highway exit?
options: a:Red with white letters,b:Yellow with black letters,c:Green with white letters
note: Guide signs that give directions, route information, and distances to exits are typically green with white lettering. These signs help drivers navigate highways and know how far it is to upcoming exits or destinations.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage (beer, wine, mixed drinks) determine how impaired you will be?
options: a:Yes — beer has no effect on reflexes,b:No — impairment depends on how much alcohol is in the bloodstream,c:Yes — mixed drinks are always more impairing than beer,d:Yes — wine is less impairing than beer
note: Impairment is determined by your blood alcohol concentration (BAC), not by whether you drink beer, wine, or liquor. A standard serving of each can contain about the same amount of alcohol, and any of them can slow your reflexes and judgment if you drink enough.

question: What is a blind spot?
options: a:The area directly behind your vehicle.,b:An area you cannot see without moving your head.,c:What you can see in your rearview mirror.
note: A blind spot is an area around your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors and must turn your head to check. These areas are usually along the sides and slightly behind your vehicle, and checking them before changing lanes or merging helps prevent collisions.

question: If you hit an unattended parked car and cannot find the owner, you must:
options: a:Wait until the police arrive and do nothing else.,b:Drive away after doing as much as you can.,c:Leave a written note with your name and contact information in a visible, secure place and report the collision as required.
note: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, you must stop, try to locate the owner, and if you cannot, leave a written note in a secure, visible place. The note should include your name, contact information, and a brief description of what happened, and you should also report the collision as required by local law.

question: A red arrow displayed on a traffic signal means:
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.,b:A driver must proceed slowly through the intersection.,c:A driver must stop and then proceed when the way is clear.
note: A red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped in the direction of that arrow. You may not turn in that direction until a green arrow or green light appears and it is safe to proceed, unless a specific sign or state law allows a turn on red and you come to a complete stop and yield first.

question: If you drink socially, what helps ensure a safe trip home?
options: a:Take a cold shower before driving.,b:Drink coffee before driving.,c:Ride with a sober friend.
note: Only a sober ride home prevents driving impaired; coffee or showers do not lower BAC.

question: An octagonal traffic sign always means:
options: a:Hospital ahead,b:Stop,c:Yield,d:Speed limit
note: The eight-sided (octagon) sign is reserved for STOP signs; approaching drivers must come to a complete stop.

question: Can there be times when 10 mph is too fast to drive safely?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Even very low speeds can be unsafe if conditions are bad enough, such as on glare ice, in dense fog, or in crowded parking areas. You must always adjust your speed to road, weather, and traffic conditions, even if that means driving much slower than the posted limit or slower than 10 mph.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:Not all railroad crossings are equipped with flashing lights and gates,b:You are allowed to go around a lowered gate if you do it quickly,c:You never need to stop for a flagger,d:Gates and lights are always present at public crossings
note: Some crossings lack gates or lights, so always be prepared to stop when approaching a crossing and obey all warnings and flaggers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Other drivers who are already in the intersection only.,b:Only to vehicles turning right.,c:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.
note: When turning left you must yield to oncoming vehicles as well as pedestrians, bicyclists, and others already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: During school hours, what is the default speed limit in a school zone unless posted otherwise?
options: a:Varies by state and posted signs; follow the posted school‑zone speed limit.,b:20 mph.,c:25 mph.
note: School‑zone speed limits are set by each state and city; there is no single default speed for all U.S. school zones. In many places the limit may be 15, 20, 25 mph, or another value, and you must always follow the posted school‑zone signs and any flashing beacons. If no special school‑zone speed is posted, you follow the regular speed limit for that road.

question: If a crossing guard directs traffic in a school zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the crossing guard's directions.,b:Follow what surrounding vehicles do instead.,c:Assume the guard has no authority.
note: Crossing guards have legal authority to direct traffic in school zones. You must obey their signals and instructions, even if they differ from traffic lights, because they are managing the safety of children and other pedestrians.

question: Which statement about driving on a wet roadway is correct?
options: a:As you drive faster, your tires become less effective at removing water.,b:Water does not affect cars with good tires.,c:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
note: On wet roads, as your speed increases, your tires have less time to squeeze water out from under the tread. This reduces traction and can lead to hydroplaning, where your tires ride on top of the water and you lose steering and braking control. Slowing down in wet conditions greatly improves tire grip.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to change lanes, which checks should you perform?
options: a:Quickly turn your head to check your blind spot only.,b:Only check your side view mirror.,c:Check side and rearview mirrors and then glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
note: Before changing lanes, first check your mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, then quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Mirrors alone do not show every vehicle; the shoulder check helps you confirm the lane is clear before you move.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are drivers required to yield to pedestrians in crosswalks?
options: a:False — drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks (this statement is false).,b:True — pedestrians always have right-of-way under all conditions.,c:True — drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked and many unmarked crosswalks at intersections.,d:False — drivers are not required to yield to pedestrians anywhere.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks and in most unmarked crosswalks at intersections, even when there are no traffic signals. You must slow or stop when necessary to allow pedestrians to cross safely, but pedestrians do not have the right‑of‑way in every possible situation, such as suddenly stepping into traffic where drivers cannot reasonably stop.

question: What color lines divide lanes moving in the same direction?
options: a:White lines.,b:Yellow lines.,c:Red lines.
note: White lines are used to separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. Broken white lines may be crossed when it is safe to change lanes or pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

question: When parallel parking between two vehicles, what should you do first?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left.,b:Turn your wheels to the right.,c:Pull up even with the vehicle directly ahead of the space.
note: When parallel parking, after you signal and check traffic, you first pull up so your vehicle is parallel and even with the vehicle ahead of the space. From that position you then begin backing into the space while turning the wheel as needed.

question: How can alcoholic beverages affect you?
options: a:They have no effect on judgment,b:They can slow reaction time,c:They only affect people who rarely drink,d:They improve coordination
note: Alcohol slows reaction time, harms judgment, and reduces coordination. These effects increase your chances of being involved in a crash, even if you feel only slightly affected.

question: How should drivers respond to a steady yellow traffic light?
options: a:Accelerate to avoid a red light.,b:Continue through only if you cannot stop safely.,c:Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You must slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when the light turns yellow, continue through with caution rather than braking abruptly.

question: If your vehicle does not have ABS and you must stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Lightly tap the brakes.,b:Firmly pump the brakes.,c:Hold the brake pedal down hard.
note: In a vehicle without ABS, you should use firm pumping of the brakes in an emergency stop. Press the brake pedal firmly, then release slightly before the wheels lock, and repeat. This helps you slow quickly while maintaining some steering control.

question: Which steps help prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Only check tread depth occasionally,b:Drive faster to cut through water,c:Ensure tires have good tread,d:Only inflate tires properly
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water instead of gripping the road. Having good tire tread, keeping tires properly inflated, and slowing down in wet conditions all help the tires cut through water and maintain contact with the pavement.

question: Which type of action is most likely to cause a crash?
options: a:Only taking your hands off the wheel,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving,c:Only taking your eyes off the road,d:Only talking to passengers
note: Anything that takes your attention away from driving—your eyes, your mind, or your hands—can greatly increase your risk of a crash. Looking away, taking your hands off the wheel, or focusing on conversations or devices are all forms of distraction that can be dangerous.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
options: a:A reflective orange triangle with a red border.,b:A circular green sign.,c:A rectangular red sign.
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle with a red border, mounted on the rear of vehicles that usually travel 25 mph or less. This emblem warns faster traffic to approach and pass with extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Does 'yield' sometimes require you to stop if you cannot merge safely?
options: a:True,b:False
note: A yield sign means you must give the right-of-way to traffic already on the road. You must slow down and be prepared to stop; if you cannot merge or cross safely, you are required to stop and wait until traffic is clear.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do?
options: a:Do not proceed until the children wave to you.,b:Watch for children walking along the side of the road before proceeding.,c:Accelerate quickly to clear the area.
note: After stopping for a school bus with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must remain stopped until the signals are turned off. When you are allowed to proceed, move slowly and watch carefully for children walking near or crossing the road.

question: A solid white line down the center of a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers should not change lanes across this line.
note: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line between lanes means lane changes are discouraged or prohibited; drivers should generally stay in their lane and not pass across it.

question: If an aggressive driver is tailing you or behaving dangerously, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to prevent them from passing,b:Brake-check them so they back off,c:Stare at the driver to intimidate them,d:Move out of their way and avoid interaction
note: When another driver is aggressive or tailgating, the safest response is to stay calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, and move out of their way when it is safe. Do not speed, brake-check, or confront them, as this can escalate the situation.

question: If your vehicle with ABS starts to lose traction, drivers should:
options: a:Pump the brakes manually.,b:Release the brake pedal immediately.,c:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
note: With antilock brakes (ABS), you should press the brake pedal firmly and hold it. The system automatically pumps the brakes to help prevent wheel lockup and allows you to steer while braking hard. Do not pump the brakes yourself.

question: Does a “Merging lanes” sign require drivers to be prepared to change lanes or allow others to merge?
options: a:True — but only on one-way streets,b:True — drivers should be prepared to change lanes or allow merging traffic,c:False — it is informational only,d:False — it indicates lane ends only
note: A merging lanes sign warns that traffic from another lane will be joining your lane. You should be prepared to adjust your speed or change lanes if needed, and allow space for merging vehicles so everyone can blend smoothly.

question: Orange-colored traffic signs typically indicate:
options: a:Work zone signs.,b:School zone signs.,c:Regulatory signs.
note: Orange traffic signs are used for temporary traffic control in work and construction zones. They warn drivers about road work, lane shifts, and other work-related conditions so drivers can slow down and proceed with extra caution.

question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?
options: a:Keep the radio off.,b:Drive slower continuously.,c:Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
note: On long trips, plan to stop regularly to rest, walk, and stretch. Short breaks help you stay alert and reduce the risk of drowsy driving. If you feel truly sleepy, the safest choice is to stop driving and take a nap or rest overnight.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your interstate exit, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly cut across lanes to reach the exit.,b:Make a sudden U-turn across traffic to reach it.,c:Continue to the next exit and do not attempt to turn around.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, stay calm, keep going, and take the next exit. Never stop, back up, cut across lanes, or make a U‑turn on the highway, as these maneuvers are extremely dangerous and illegal in most places.

question: At an intersection, what does a flashing red light require you to do?
options: a:Stop only if traffic is present.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

question: About how much alcohol does the average person's body process per hour?
options: a:One drink an hour.,b:Two drinks an hour.,c:Three drinks an hour.
note: The body typically processes alcohol at about the rate of one standard drink per hour, though this varies by person. Drinking faster than your body can process alcohol increases your blood alcohol concentration and your level of impairment, even if you feel fine.

question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.,b:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,c:Checking your antifreeze and washer fluid is important.
note: You should never use cruise control on snow, ice, or other slippery winter surfaces because it can cause you to lose control if the vehicle starts to skid. Winter is generally one of the most difficult driving seasons, and checking items like antifreeze and washer fluid is important for safe operation.

question: Who is required to use a properly fastened safety belt in Utah?
options: a:Only the driver,b:Only passengers younger than 16,c:Only passengers older than 18,d:All occupants of the vehicle
note: In Utah, everyone in a vehicle must use a properly fastened safety belt or an approved child restraint. The driver can be cited if they or any passenger under 16 is not properly restrained, and passengers 16 and older can be cited for not wearing their own seat belts.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a 'Merging traffic' sign on the freeway, you should:
options: a:Make room by changing lanes or adjusting speed to allow merging traffic.,b:Honk at incoming traffic.,c:Always remain at your present speed.
note: When you see a merging traffic sign, you should help traffic enter safely by adjusting your speed and, when possible, changing lanes away from the merge area. Never honk or try to block merging vehicles; cooperative merging reduces crashes and keeps traffic flowing smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far must you be able to be seen from both directions before making a U-turn?
options: a:200 feet.,b:500 feet.,c:100 feet.
note: You must not make a U-turn where other drivers cannot see you from at least 500 feet in both directions, such as near the top of a hill or on a curve. This distance gives approaching drivers enough time to see you and react safely.

question: When backing up, how should you check behind your vehicle?
options: a:Flash your lights continuously while backing,b:Rely solely on mirrors and sensors,c:Open your door and step out every time,d:Turn and look through the rear window over your shoulder and do not rely only on mirrors
note: When backing, turn your body and look directly through the rear window over your shoulder so you can see the area behind your vehicle. Use mirrors and sensors only as helpers; they do not show everything and can miss children, pedestrians, or small objects.

question: At night when another vehicle approaches from the opposite direction, your headlights should be:
options: a:Turned off and use parking lights.,b:Set to high beam.,c:Set to low beam.
note: At night, switch to low-beam headlights when an oncoming vehicle is approaching so you do not blind the other driver. High beams can cause glare and make it hard for the other driver to see the road, increasing the risk of a collision.

question: A red flashing traffic light has the same meaning as a:
options: a:Solid red light.,b:Stop sign.,c:Yield sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must treat the intersection like a stop sign: come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: A child under eight years old and shorter than what height must be in an approved child safety seat?
options: a:72 inches,b:60 inches,c:57 inches
note: In Utah, children under eight years old who are shorter than 57 inches must ride in an approved child safety seat or booster until the vehicle’s seat belt fits them properly across the shoulder and lap.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on an interstate, before changing lanes you should:
options: a:Always use cruise control.,b:Signal,c:Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
note: Before changing lanes on an interstate, always signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check blind spots. Stopping on the shoulder is only for emergencies, not for routine lane changes.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicate?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.,b:Passing is allowed from either direction.,c:Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line, and not allowed from the side with the solid line. Drivers on the broken-line side may pass when it is safe.

question: How does a wet or icy road affect stopping distance?
options: a:It only affects stopping at night.,b:It decreases stopping distance.,c:It increases stopping distance.
note: Wet, icy, or otherwise slippery roads reduce traction, so it takes more time and distance to stop. You should slow down and increase your following distance because stopping distance increases on these surfaces.

question: If someone has consumed alcohol, which remedy will help them sober up quickly?
options: a:Fresh air and exercise will sober them up quickly,b:Tomato juice will speed sobriety,c:Only the passage of time will eliminate the influence of alcohol,d:Hot coffee will remove alcohol from the bloodstream
note: Nothing speeds the elimination of alcohol from the body except time; coffee, fresh air, or other remedies do not reduce blood alcohol concentration.

question: A properly adjusted seat belt should fit how?
options: a:Is loose.,b:Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and low on your abdomen, with the shoulder belt across the center of your chest.,c:Is hidden beneath the seat.
note: A lap belt should be snug across the hip bones and low on the abdomen, never across the stomach alone. The strong pelvic bones help absorb crash forces and reduce the risk of internal injuries. The shoulder belt should cross the center of the chest and rest on the shoulder, not the neck or under the arm.

question: What is true about drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving?
options: a:They are better drivers because they are more cautious than sober drivers.,b:They are always fully aware of the risks they are taking.,c:They do not have sufficient control over their bodies and driving abilities.
note: Drivers who have been drinking lose judgment, coordination, and reaction time, so they cannot control their bodies or vehicles as well as when sober. Even small amounts of alcohol reduce the ability to steer, brake, and respond to hazards safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-way, two-lane road, when is passing unsafe?
options: a:When the car ahead is disabled.,b:When you are turning into a driveway.,c:When you cannot return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic or without interfering with other vehicles.
note: Passing is unsafe any time you cannot complete the pass and return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic. You must be able to see far enough ahead, judge that you have enough space and speed to pass, and return to your lane without forcing oncoming vehicles or the car you are passing to slow or swerve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Drivers may proceed without stopping if they feel safe,b:The first vehicle to arrive should proceed first,c:The vehicle on the left always goes first,d:The last vehicle to arrive has priority
note: At a four-way stop, every driver must come to a complete stop. The vehicle that arrives first has the right-of-way and should go first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first. When in doubt, communicate with eye contact and hand signals and proceed cautiously.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on a highway divided by two solid yellow lines. Which action is allowed?
options: a:Cross these lines to pass other vehicles,b:Cross these lines under no circumstances.,c:Cross these lines only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, driveway, or side street
note: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing in either direction. You may not cross them to pass another vehicle. You may only cross double solid yellow lines when you are making a left turn into or from a driveway, alley, side road, or private road, and only when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: Defensive driving means:
options: a:Following the vehicle ahead at a close distance.,b:Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.,c:Defending yourself by getting ahead of poor drivers in traffic.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road for potential hazards and being prepared to react early. This includes watching other drivers, road conditions, and traffic signals so you can slow down, change lanes, or stop in time to avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?
options: a:Whoever started moving last,b:The pedestrian must yield to the turning vehicle,c:The driver turning must yield to the pedestrian,d:The vehicle that is slower must yield
note: When turning, drivers must yield to pedestrians who are legally crossing the street, even if there is no traffic light. Slow down or stop as needed so the pedestrian can cross safely before you complete your turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to stop or park on the shoulder of a freeway?
options: a:Any time if you turn on emergency flashers,b:If part of the vehicle is off the roadway,c:To check a map or get directions,d:Only in an emergency
note: On freeways, stopping or parking on the shoulder is only allowed for emergencies, such as a breakdown or medical issue. If you must stop, pull as far onto the shoulder as possible, turn on your hazard lights, and stay safe away from moving traffic.

question: When driving in poor weather, what should you do to maintain safety?
options: a:Tailgate slower vehicles to encourage them to speed up,b:Increase your following distance to allow more stopping time,c:Decrease your following distance to get off the road quicker,d:Maintain the same following distance as in clear weather
note: In poor weather, such as rain, fog, or snow, it takes longer to see hazards and to stop. Increasing your following distance gives you more time and space to react if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.

question: What does a single dashed white line separating traffic indicate?
options: a:Lanes moving in the same direction that may be crossed to pass.,b:Drivers may not pass under any circumstances.,c:Lanes move in opposite directions.
note: A single dashed white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, how should you position your front wheels?
options: a:Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb and let the vehicle roll back slightly until the tire gently touches the curb. This way, if your brakes fail, the curb will stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:
options: a:Turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.,b:Close the door and leave the engine running.,c:Leave the key in the ignition for a short time.
note: When leaving a vehicle unattended, stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

question: Nighttime is the safest time for cyclists to ride their bikes.
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Nighttime is more dangerous for cyclists because they are harder for drivers to see, even with lights and reflectors. Riding in daylight and using proper lighting and reflective gear at all times improves safety.

question: If you see an animal on the road, what should you do?
options: a:Pass as closely as possible to clear the way.,b:Ignore it and maintain speed.,c:Pass slowly and cautiously to avoid startling it.
note: When you see an animal on or near the road, slow down and pass it cautiously. Moving slowly and giving it space helps prevent the animal from being startled and darting unpredictably into your path.

question: If another driver cuts you off, the best immediate reaction is to:
options: a:Flash your high beams at the driver.,b:Let it go and continue driving safely.,c:Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
note: If another driver cuts you off, stay calm and avoid reacting with anger. Do not try to get even, yell, or signal aggressively, because this can quickly escalate into road rage and create a dangerous situation. The safest response is to let it go, slow slightly if needed to re‑establish a safe following distance, and continue driving defensively.

question: If a train is near enough to be dangerous, what must you do?
options: a:Not cross the tracks until the train has fully passed.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Cross the tracks if no signals are active.
note: If a train is close enough to be dangerous, you must not cross the tracks. Trains cannot stop quickly, and they always have the right of way. Stay stopped until the train has completely passed and you can clearly see that no other train is coming, then proceed only when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: A flashing red traffic signal means:
options: a:The traffic signal is broken.,b:The same thing as a stop sign.,c:You do not have to come to a complete stop.
note: A flashing red traffic signal is treated exactly like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then yield to other traffic and pedestrians. Proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe to go.

question: A Class D license authorizes you to operate a vehicle that weighs up to which of the following?
options: a:26,000 pounds.,b:36,000 pounds.,c:33,000 pounds.,d:40,000 pounds.
note: A Class D regular operator license permits operation of personal vehicles up to 26,000 pounds GVWR; heavier vehicles require a different class of license.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped by a police officer, you should:
options: a:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.,b:Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.,c:Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
note: When stopped by a police officer, you should safely pull over, put the vehicle in park, keep your seat belt fastened, and stay inside with your hands clearly visible on the steering wheel. Wait for the officer to approach and ask for your license, registration, and insurance before reaching for anything. Sudden movements or reaching around before the officer arrives can be misinterpreted and create safety concerns.

question: A single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers may pass when it is safe.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: A single broken white line separates lanes moving in the same direction. You may change lanes or pass another vehicle when it is safe and legal to do so, checking mirrors and blind spots first.

question: Before switching on the ignition you should:
options: a:Buckle your safety belt and ensure all passengers have done likewise.,b:Be sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.,c:Be sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
note: Develop a routine to buckle your own seat belt and confirm that all passengers are belted before starting the vehicle.

question: What does a single dashed yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,b:Drivers may pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Drivers may not pass at any time.
note: A single dashed yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions. You may pass when it is safe, with enough clear distance ahead, and without interfering with oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals at an intersection are out due to a power outage, you should:
options: a:Park and wait for power to be restored.,b:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop and proceed when it is your turn.,c:Use hand signals to direct traffic.
note: When traffic signals are not working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Come to a complete stop, then proceed in turn: first vehicle to stop goes first, and if two arrive together, the driver on the right goes first. Always move through the intersection cautiously and be prepared to yield.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Never move it under any circumstances,b:Move it off the traveled portion of the roadway,c:Wait for police to move it for you,d:Leave it and walk away
note: If you are in a minor crash and your vehicle can be driven, move it out of the traffic lane to the shoulder or a safe area. This helps prevent additional collisions. Stay at the scene, exchange information, and provide aid if needed.

question: As a pedestrian, what is the safest action when vehicles are approaching?
options: a:Enter a crosswalk at any time because drivers must stop.,b:Always insist on the right-of-way over a vehicle when in a crosswalk.,c:Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
note: Do not enter a street or crosswalk if vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a nearby vehicle may not be able to stop in time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs indicate?
options: a:Potential driving speeds for the area.,b:The maximum or minimum speed that is legally allowed to be driven.,c:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic.
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum (and sometimes minimum) speed that is legally allowed under ideal conditions. You must slow down below the posted limit when conditions such as rain, fog, traffic, or road work make it unsafe to travel that fast.

question: If you are being tailgated, what is the best response?
options: a:Accelerate to increase the gap.,b:Move to the right if possible; if not, slow gradually when safe to encourage the tailgater to pass.,c:Brake abruptly to teach them a lesson.,d:Ignore them and maintain your speed no matter what.
note: When someone is following too closely, the safest response is to move to the right lane or another safe space so they can pass. If you cannot move over, slow down gradually to increase your following distance ahead and encourage the tailgater to go around you. Never brake suddenly, because that increases the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: On slippery roads you should:
options: a:Drive as you would on dry roads.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Use alternate routes.
note: On slippery roads, your tires have less traction and it takes much longer to stop. You should increase your following distance so you have more time and space to brake gently and avoid skidding. Sudden moves, including hard braking or sharp steering, are more likely to cause a loss of control on slick surfaces.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:When entering a street from a garage, driveway, or alley.,b:When your traffic signal is a green arrow.,c:When they are on a road to your right and you have reached an unmarked intersection at the same time.
note: When you enter a street from a driveway, alley, or garage, you must stop if necessary and yield to all traffic on the roadway and to pedestrians on the sidewalk. Vehicles already on the road have the right-of-way. A green arrow generally gives you the right-of-way for that movement after yielding to any traffic or pedestrians still in the intersection, and at an unmarked intersection you must yield to vehicles on your right, not your left.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:Carbon monoxide poisoning.,b:A loss of hearing.,c:Pollution.
note: A leaky exhaust system is dangerous because it can allow carbon monoxide, a colorless and odorless poisonous gas, to enter the passenger compartment. Breathing carbon monoxide can cause headache, dizziness, unconsciousness, and even death. Any exhaust leak should be repaired immediately to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal means which light will soon appear?
options: a:A flashing red will soon appear,b:A steady green will soon appear,c:A steady red light will soon appear,d:A flashing yellow will soon appear
note: A steady yellow traffic signal warns that the light is about to turn red. You should slow down and prepare to stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely when the light changes.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign generally:
options: a:Alerts drivers to school zones.,b:Alerts drivers to public recreation areas.,c:Warns of existing or possible hazards.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are general warning signs. They alert drivers to existing or possible hazards on or near the roadway, such as curves, intersections, merging traffic, or road work. School zones and recreation areas have their own specific sign shapes and symbols, but the diamond shape itself means a warning.

question: If confronted by an aggressive driver, what is the recommended response?
options: a:Engage in an argument at the next stop,b:Avoid eye contact,c:Cut them off to slow them down,d:Retaliate by tailgating them
note: If you encounter an aggressive driver, stay calm and do not engage. Avoid eye contact, do not respond with rude gestures or actions, and do not try to block or race them. Safely slow down, move over if needed, and let them pass. If you feel threatened, seek a safe place and contact law enforcement.

question: When a traffic signal turns green, what should you do first?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and any traffic still in the intersection.,b:Accelerate as fast as possible.,c:Back up slowly.
note: When a traffic signal turns green, you may proceed only after first checking the intersection and yielding to pedestrians and any vehicles still in the intersection. A green light means you have the right to go if the way is clear, not that you should immediately accelerate without looking.

question: A driver should never pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. Is this true?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must never pass a vehicle that is stopped at a crosswalk because there may be pedestrians crossing in front of that vehicle whom you cannot see. Passing in this situation can lead to hitting someone who steps out from in front of the stopped car.

question: If a traffic signal turns from green to solid yellow as you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to get through before it turns red.,b:Treat it the same as a caution sign and continue.,c:Stop before entering the intersection unless you are too close to stop safely.
note: A solid yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop without hard braking that could cause a crash, continue through the intersection with caution.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb on a two-way street, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Keep your wheels straight,b:Turn so the rear wheel rests on the curb,c:Turn your steering wheel to the left so the front right tire rests against the curb,d:Turn your steering wheel to the right
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb (to the left when parked on the right side of a two‑way street). If your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll back and the front right tire will gently contact the curb, helping stop the car and keeping it from rolling into traffic.

question: You are involved in an accident. Which immediate action is required?
options: a:Help the injured.,b:Call the police.,c:Stop immediately.
note: If you are involved in a crash, the law requires that you stop immediately at or near the scene. Once stopped and safe from traffic, you should check for injuries, call emergency services, and provide reasonable help to anyone who is hurt.

question: How can you avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Simply say you will not drink if someone offers you a drink.,b:Call a taxi only after you start drinking.,c:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.
note: The best way to avoid an alcohol‑related crash is to decide before you start drinking that you will not drive afterward. Plan ahead for a sober driver, taxi, rideshare, or other transportation so you are never tempted to drive after drinking.

question: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings:
options: a:Are merely suggestions.,b:Must always be obeyed.,c:Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings are traffic control devices that you are legally required to obey. Ignoring them can cause crashes and traffic violations because they tell you when to stop, go, yield, and how to position your vehicle on the road.

question: A red traffic signal means you must:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop before entering the intersection or crosswalk.,c:Stop only if pedestrians are present.
note: A steady red traffic signal means you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, or before entering the crosswalk or intersection if there is no stop line. You must remain stopped until the light turns green and it is safe to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Do pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections always have the right-of-way?
options: a:False — pedestrians have the right-of-way in many situations, but not always (for example, when they disobey traffic signals),b:True — they always do under all conditions,c:False — drivers always have the right-of-way,d:True — except at marked crosswalks
note: Pedestrians usually have the right-of-way in marked and unmarked crosswalks, but they must also obey traffic signals and signs. A pedestrian who crosses against a red light or "DON'T WALK" signal does not have the right-of-way, and drivers are not required to yield in that situation, though they must still do everything possible to avoid a collision.

question: What defines an inattentive driver?
options: a:Watching only the vehicle directly ahead of them.,b:Maintaining eye contact with a passenger during a conversation.,c:Daydreaming or staring at objects off the roadway while driving.,d:Any driver whose attention is diverted from the road, including by daydreaming, conversations, or looking at objects off the roadway.
note: An inattentive driver is anyone whose mind or eyes are not focused on the driving task. This includes daydreaming, staring at objects off the roadway, or being distracted by passengers, devices, or other activities. Looking away from the road or mentally checking out greatly increases the risk of missing hazards and reacting too late.

question: When may you cross solid yellow lines?
options: a:To pass traffic moving in your direction.,b:Only to make a turn.,c:At any time of day.
note: A solid yellow line generally means you may not cross it to pass another vehicle. However, you are usually allowed to cross a solid yellow line when making a left turn into or out of a driveway, side road, or alley, as long as it is safe and not otherwise prohibited by signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing another vehicle you should:
options: a:Signal after changing lanes.,b:Signal early enough for other drivers to know your intentions.,c:Signal just before changing lanes.
note: Before passing or changing lanes, you must signal early enough to give other drivers time to see your signal and react. Turn on your signal, check your mirrors, quickly check your blind spot, and only then move into the other lane when it is safe.

question: How should you check your blind spot when changing lanes to the left?
options: a:Turn on your left turn signal and rely on it,b:Look straight ahead only,c:Check your right side mirror,d:Glance over your left shoulder
note: When changing lanes to the left, first signal, check your mirrors, and then quickly glance over your left shoulder to check the blind spot. This over-the-shoulder check lets you see vehicles that do not appear in your mirrors.

question: When making a turn, you must do what with your speed?
options: a:Reduce it so you can maintain control.,b:Increase it to clear the intersection.,c:Keep it unchanged.
note: Before turning, slow to a safe speed so you can stay in your lane and keep control of the vehicle throughout the turn. Enter the turn at a reduced speed, then gently accelerate as you complete it if conditions allow.

question: How should you regard railroad crossings?
options: a:Safe places to park a car.,b:Dangerous and always approached with caution.,c:Safe to cross because trains are unlikely.
note: Railroad crossings are always potentially dangerous and must be approached with caution. Slow down, look and listen for trains, obey all warning signs and signals, and never stop or park on the tracks.

question: What does the term “No zone” refer to around large vehicles?
options: a:A lane closed for construction,b:A roadway where stereo systems are restricted,c:Areas of reduced visibility (blind spots) around trucks and buses,d:A special speed zone
note: The “No zone” is the large blind-spot area around trucks and buses where the driver cannot see you in the mirrors. Avoid lingering in these areas, especially directly behind, alongside the sides near the cab, and close in front of the truck.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing without flashing warning signals or gates, you should:
options: a:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,b:Prepare to yield to any approaching train at the crossing.,c:Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.
note: At a railroad crossing without active signals or gates, you must slow, look, and listen for trains and be prepared to stop. You only proceed when you are sure no train is approaching and it is safe to cross. You are not required to always stop if no train is coming, but you must be ready to yield to any train, since trains always have the right-of-way.

question: A “Reduced speed, 35 mph” sign indicates what?
options: a:The reduced speed sign is advisory only and begins after the next sign,b:You have plenty of distance to slow down before the zone,c:The reduced speed applies only if police are present,d:The new speed limit of 35 mph begins at that sign
note: When you see a regulatory "Reduced speed, 35 mph" sign, the new speed limit begins at that sign. You must slow to 35 mph by the time you reach the sign and obey that limit from that point on, unless another sign changes it.

question: What is the legal BAC limit to drive in Utah?
options: a:0.08 percent.,b:0.02 percent.,c:0.05 percent.
note: In Utah, the per se legal limit for most adult drivers is 0.05% BAC. That means you can be charged with DUI at or above 0.05%. However, you can still be arrested for impaired driving at lower levels if your ability to drive safely is affected.

question: What is the only effective way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Allow your body time to eliminate the alcohol.,b:Drink coffee to sober up.,c:Exercise to speed alcohol removal.
note: Only time removes alcohol from your system; coffee, showers, and exercise do not lower BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you start a left turn on a multilane one-way street or highway?
options: a:Start from the middle of the intersection.,b:Start from the left lane.,c:Start from the right lane.
note: On a multilane one-way street or highway, you should start a left turn from the leftmost lane that is lawfully available. Positioning in the left lane before turning reduces conflicts with other traffic and helps you turn safely into the correct lane on the new road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you slow down when exiting a highway?
options: a:After you have moved into the exit lane.,b:On the main road, just before the exit lane.,c:Once you see a toll booth.
note: On highways, you should maintain the normal traffic speed in the main travel lane and move into the exit (deceleration) lane before you begin to slow down. Braking in the main lane can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear‑end collision. Once fully in the exit lane, reduce speed as needed for the ramp and any posted advisory speed signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a highway from an entrance ramp, you should generally:
options: a:Merge without signaling to move quickly,b:Enter very slowly to avoid disturbing traffic,c:Accelerate to match the speed of traffic and merge when safe,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a clear gap
note: Use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to get up to the speed of traffic on the highway, signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge when there is a safe gap. Entering too slowly or stopping at the end of the ramp can cause dangerous speed differences and rear‑end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what circumstance may you cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To pass a slow-moving truck.,b:To pass another car.,c:To turn into a driveway or to make a left turn where permitted.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean vehicles in both directions are prohibited from passing. However, you may carefully cross them to make a left turn into or from a driveway, side road, alley, or other place where left turns are allowed, after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is traveling in your area, you should:
options: a:Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.,b:Stop your vehicle immediately and prevent them from passing.,c:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right‑of‑way. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop, or otherwise position your vehicle so the emergency vehicle has a clear path. Never speed up or block their way; your goal is to give them room to pass quickly and safely.

question: How can you ensure your physical condition doesn't impair your driving?
options: a:Only drive when feeling perfectly rested.,b:Know medicine effects,c:Drive faster to reduce exposure time.
note: To avoid your physical condition impairing your driving, you must understand how any medicines you take—prescription, over‑the‑counter, or recreational—affect alertness, vision, and reaction time. Combine this with honest awareness of fatigue, illness, or other health issues, and delay or avoid driving if they could make you unsafe.

question: Is it true that the faster your speed, the longer it takes to stop?
options: a:Only true for heavy vehicles,b:Only true when roads are wet,c:False,d:True
note: As your speed increases, both your reaction distance (how far you travel before you start braking) and your braking distance (how far you travel after you start braking) increase. This means the faster you go, the longer it takes to stop, regardless of vehicle type or weather.

question: Which of the following is a recommended practice for driving safely at night?
options: a:Make sure your headlights are working properly.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Do not drive if you are tired.,d:All of the above are good night‑driving safety practices.
note: At night, visibility is reduced and it is harder to see hazards in time. You should increase your following distance so you have more time to react and stop safely. It is also important to make sure your headlights work properly and to avoid driving when you are tired, but increasing following distance is the key night‑driving technique emphasized in this question.

question: How should you drive on slippery roads?
options: a:Maintain posted speed regardless of conditions,b:Slow down and drive more cautiously than the posted speed,c:Drive faster to get through quickly,d:Tailgate the vehicle ahead to reduce spray
note: On slippery roads, such as when it is raining, icy, or snowy, you must slow down below the posted speed limit and drive smoothly. The posted speed is for ideal conditions; when traction is reduced, you need extra time and distance to stop and to avoid skidding.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing that only has a crossbuck sign, you should:
options: a:Approach all tracks with extreme caution and cross only when you know no train is coming.,b:Turn your radio down and open a window to help you hear if a train is approaching.,c:Only continue once cleared to do so by a flagger, if applicable.,d:Stop at least 15 feet from the tracks at every crossbuck, even if no train is visible.
note: A crossbuck sign marks a railroad crossing and means you must yield to trains. Approach the tracks with extreme caution, look and listen for trains in both directions, and only cross when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely. Trains always have the right of way.

question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and slash indicate?
options: a:That some drivers must yield to others.,b:That the specified action is prohibited.,c:That drivers should come to a complete stop.
note: A regulatory sign with a red circle and a diagonal slash over a symbol means that the action shown is not allowed. For example, a right‑turn arrow with a red circle and slash means "No Right Turn." These signs tell drivers which specific actions are prohibited.

question: When should you use your headlights due to limited visibility?
options: a:Only at night.,b:Only when you can see 500 feet ahead.,c:Any time conditions prevent you from seeing at least 1,000 feet ahead.
note: Turn on your headlights whenever visibility is poor so you can see and be seen. In many states, you must use headlights when you cannot clearly see people or vehicles at 1,000 feet, and also from sunset to sunrise or when using windshield wipers for rain, snow, or fog.

question: How should you pass a bicyclist safely?
options: a:Honk to alert the bicyclist to move over.,b:Drive in the bike lane until you can pass.,c:Slow down and give as much space as possible.
note: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and give them plenty of space. Many states require at least 3 feet of clearance, and more at higher speeds. Do not honk aggressively, crowd the bicyclist, or drive in the bike lane to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following takes precedence over the others?
options: a:A police officer directing traffic,b:A steady red light,c:A stop sign,d:Pavement markings
note: Instructions from a police officer or other authorized person directing traffic always override traffic lights, signs, and pavement markings. You must follow the officer’s directions, even if they conflict with the normal traffic controls.

question: If you have a tire blowout while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Keep accelerating to maintain control,b:Slam on your brakes immediately,c:Ease off the accelerator,d:Turn the vehicle off while moving
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly and ease off the accelerator to slow down gradually. Avoid hard braking, keep the vehicle going straight, and when under control, carefully move to the side of the road and stop in a safe place.

question: What color are guide/destination signs and their lettering?
options: a:Yellow background with black letters,b:Green background with white letters,c:Red background with white letters
note: Guide and destination signs are typically green with white letters or symbols. They provide information such as directions, distances, and locations of cities, exits, and services.

question: When interacting with pedestrians, a driver must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.,b:Always yield the right-of-way,c:Make sure the pedestrian is aware of their vehicle.
note: Drivers must do everything possible to avoid striking pedestrians and should yield to them even if they are crossing where they should not be.

question: If a pedestrian starts crossing in front of you, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your lights to warn them to hurry.,b:Speed up and pass ahead of them.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop
note: If a pedestrian begins crossing in front of you, you must slow down and be prepared to stop. Drivers are required to yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and should never try to speed up or pressure them to hurry. Reducing speed and being ready to stop helps prevent collisions and protects vulnerable road users.

question: As alcohol builds up in your bloodstream, it:
options: a:Begins to metabolize itself more quickly.,b:Makes you feel less confident.,c:Slows down your reactions.
note: As alcohol builds up in your bloodstream, it slows your reaction time and impairs judgment. You may feel more confident or less inhibited, but your ability to notice hazards, make good decisions, and react quickly is reduced, which makes driving dangerous.

question: How must drivers respond to a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended and red lights flashing?
options: a:Proceed if you think children are clear,b:Slow down and pass carefully,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the bus resumes motion or the stop arm is withdrawn,d:Honk to alert any children
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, drivers in most situations must come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn or the bus moves again. This protects children who may be crossing the road and can be unpredictable.

question: What should motorists do when driving near a cyclist?
options: a:Honk to make the cyclist move over,b:Share the lane without increasing following distance,c:Maintain a safe operating distance and be especially cautious,d:Assume the cyclist will yield right-of-way
note: When driving near a cyclist, you must maintain a safe distance and use extra caution. Give the cyclist plenty of room when passing, avoid crowding the lane, and be prepared for them to swerve to avoid hazards. Treat bicycles as legitimate vehicles sharing the road.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Maintain your current speed and steer straight.,b:Try to steer straight while gradually slowing by removing your foot from the gas pedal.,c:Brake hard immediately.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle going straight, and gradually slow down by easing your foot off the accelerator. Avoid hard braking, because sudden braking can cause you to lose control, especially at higher speeds. Once the vehicle has slowed and you have it under control, gently brake as needed and move off the roadway to a safe place.

question: On a divided multilane highway when an emergency vehicle approaches, how should you respond?
options: a:Move safely to the right side of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.,b:Disregard the signal if other lanes are available.,c:Slow down.
note: On a divided multilane highway, when an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right-of-way by moving as far to the right as you safely can and stopping until it has passed. Simply slowing down is not enough; you must create a clear path and stop unless directed otherwise by law enforcement or it is physically impossible to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is the posted maximum speed limit always the fastest safe speed you can drive?
options: a:True,b:False
note: The posted maximum speed limit is the fastest legal speed only under ideal conditions. You must always adjust your speed to road, traffic, and weather conditions. If the road is wet, visibility is poor, or traffic is heavy, it is often unsafe and illegal to drive at the posted maximum.

question: When driving in rain, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: In rain, use low beam headlights. Low beams help you see the road and make your vehicle more visible to others without causing glare or reflecting too much light back at you from the rain. High beams can create glare and reduce your ability to see in wet conditions.

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical effect of drinking alcohol?
options: a:Slower reflexes and reaction time.,b:Increased alertness.,c:Distorted judgement of speed and distance.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain and body functions. It typically causes slower reflexes, reduced alertness, and poor judgment of speed, distance, and risk. It does not make you more alert or improve your driving ability at any level of impairment.

question: Should you use high beam headlights while driving in fog?
options: a:No — high beams can reflect back and reduce visibility (True),b:Yes — high beams improve visibility in fog (False),c:Either is fine depending on the road,d:Use high beams with fog lights
note: In fog, you should use low beam headlights or dedicated fog lights. High beams shine light higher and more broadly, which reflects off the water droplets in fog and creates glare, making it harder to see. Low beams aim light lower toward the road surface and reduce reflection, improving your ability to see lane lines and the edge of the road.

question: What do pentagonal (five-sided) road signs indicate?
options: a:Speed limits.,b:School zones.,c:No passing zones.
note: Pentagon-shaped (five-sided) signs are used for school zones and school crossings. When you see a pentagonal sign, slow down, watch for children, and be prepared to stop for pedestrians in or near the roadway.

question: Orange signs in work zones indicate what?
options: a:They indicate scenic routes,b:They mark parking restrictions,c:They warn drivers of construction or maintenance work areas,d:They designate school zones
note: Orange signs are used in work zones to warn drivers about construction, maintenance, or utility work areas. They alert you to changing road conditions, workers, equipment, lane shifts, and reduced speeds so you can slow down and proceed with extra caution.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and wait for the light to change.,b:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.,c:Drive carefully through the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow traffic signal means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop, but you should be prepared to yield to pedestrians and cross traffic that has the right-of-way.

question: What type of sign requires drivers to obey the instruction it indicates?
options: a:Warning signs.,b:Information signs.,c:Regulatory signs.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do, such as speed limits, stop, yield, and no-turn signs. These signs are enforceable by law, and you are required to obey their instructions.

question: How do blind spots change with vehicle size?
options: a:Larger vehicles have smaller blind spots,b:Large vehicles have no blind spots due to mirrors,c:Larger vehicles have larger blind spots,d:All vehicles have the same blind spot size
note: Larger vehicles such as trucks, vans, and SUVs have bigger blind spots than smaller cars. Their height and length create larger areas around the front, rear, and sides where other road users cannot be seen in the mirrors, so you should avoid lingering alongside or close behind them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may cautiously continue through an intersection with a yellow light if:
options: a:There are pedestrians crossing.,b:An emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.,c:You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should continue through carefully. If you have not yet entered and can stop safely before the intersection, you are expected to stop rather than speed up to beat the red.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle under which conditions?
options: a:Where there is a red light only.,b:At a stop sign.,c:At an intersection with a stop sign only.
note: You must come to a complete stop at every stop sign, at red lights (including flashing red), and whenever a traffic officer or school crossing guard orders you to stop. A stop sign always requires a full stop before the crosswalk or limit line, even if you think the way is clear.

question: If you must drive in fog, you should:
options: a:Drive at the maximum posted speed.,b:Turn on your low-beam headlights.,c:Use your hazard lights.
note: In fog, slow down and use low‑beam headlights so you can see and be seen without glare reflecting back at you. High beams and hazard lights can make it harder for you and others to see. If visibility is extremely poor, be prepared to pull off the road to a safe location and wait for conditions to improve.

question: Road surfaces are especially slippery during which period of a rainstorm?
options: a:When it has been raining for an hour or more.,b:The day after it rains.,c:For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
note: Roads are usually most slippery during the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm. Water mixes with oil and other residues on the pavement, creating a slick surface. Reduce your speed, increase following distance, and avoid hard braking or sharp turns during this period.

question: Which road condition most affects your ability to stop?
options: a:The condition of the road surface.,b:Signal lights.,c:The time of day.
note: Road surface condition is one of the biggest factors in how quickly you can stop. Wet, icy, or loose gravel surfaces reduce traction, increasing your stopping distance even if your brakes and reactions are good.

question: Which of the following can impair a person's ability to drive?
options: a:Prescription medications, over‑the‑counter drugs, and illegal drugs,b:Alcohol,c:Being very tired or drowsy,d:All of the above can impair driving
note: Alcohol, many prescription and over‑the‑counter medications, illegal drugs, and being very tired can all slow your reactions and judgment. Any substance or condition that affects your mind or body can impair driving, not just alcohol or illegal drugs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While waiting in an intersection to complete a left turn, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels straight so you won’t be pushed into oncoming traffic if struck from behind,b:Signal and keep your wheels turned left,c:Flash headlights to warn oncoming drivers,d:Honk to get other drivers to stop
note: When waiting to turn left, keep your front wheels straight. If another vehicle hits you from behind, straight wheels help prevent your car from being pushed into oncoming traffic. Turn the wheels only as you actually begin the turn.

question: What is the most common color for warning signs?
options: a:Yellow,b:Green,c:Red
note: Most general warning signs are yellow with black symbols or lettering and are often diamond‑shaped. They alert you to conditions such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings ahead so you can slow down and be prepared.

question: Under what conditions may you drive around a lowered railroad gate?
options: a:If you can see there is no train approaching,b:Under no circumstances,c:Only when the lights stop flashing,d:When the train has passed and the gate is fully raised
note: You must never drive around or under a lowered railroad gate. Even if you do not see a train, signals can be activated before a train is visible and trains take a long distance to stop. Only cross after the train has passed, the lights stop flashing, the gate is fully raised, and you have checked that the tracks are clear.

question: What is the single most effective action to reduce your risk of serious injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Limit driving to weekdays.,b:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.,c:Wear your seat belt.
note: Wearing a seat belt is the single most effective way to reduce the risk of death or serious injury in a crash. Seat belts keep you from being thrown from the vehicle, spread crash forces over stronger parts of your body, and help you stay in position to control the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When turning left into a driveway.,b:When the car ahead is disabled.,c:When crossing would interfere with other traffic.
note: A single broken line (white between same-direction lanes, yellow between opposite-direction lanes) may be crossed to pass or change lanes only when it is safe. It is illegal to cross if doing so would interfere with other traffic, such as forcing others to brake or swerve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you wish to turn but are not in the proper lane, you should:
options: a:Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.,b:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.,c:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
note: If you are not in the correct lane for a turn when you reach an intersection, you must go straight, then continue to the next intersection and get into the proper lane before turning. Sudden lane changes or cutting across traffic can cause crashes, and turning from the wrong lane is illegal in many situations.

question: When approaching a steady green traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Continue driving unless there are vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Stop if a police officer is nearby.,c:Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, if it is safe, but you must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection. Approach at a speed that allows you to stop safely if the light changes to yellow or red.

question: Is parking in handicap access aisles next to accessible stalls allowed?
options: a:True — if you have a permit,b:True — for short stops only,c:False — parking in handicap access aisles is prohibited,d:True — if nobody is using the access aisle
note: Handicap access aisles next to accessible parking spaces must always be kept clear so people using wheelchairs, lifts, or other mobility devices can safely enter and exit vehicles. It is illegal to park or stop in these striped access aisles, even with a disability placard or for a short time.

question: What is a common cause of crashes?
options: a:Consistently checking mirrors and blind spots.,b:Yielding the right-of-way correctly.,c:Driving too fast for conditions.
note: Driving too fast for conditions is one of the most common causes of crashes. Even if you are under the posted speed limit, you must slow down when roads are wet, icy, foggy, or visibility is reduced, or when traffic is heavy. Safe drivers adjust their speed to match current conditions.

question: Driving while distracted usually causes the driver to:
options: a:React more quickly to hazards.,b:React more slowly to hazards.,c:Drive faster than usual.
note: Distractions such as phones, passengers, or adjusting controls take your attention away from the road. This delays how quickly you notice hazards and how fast you can react, which greatly increases your chances of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing is prohibited in which places?
options: a:On hills,b:At intersections only.,c:On hills and curves only.
note: Passing in locations where visibility or safety is limited (hills, curves, intersections, railroad crossings) is unlawful and unsafe.

question: A common telltale sign of a drunk driver is:
options: a:Driving more slowly than the normal traffic flow.,b:Weaving between lanes.,c:Making quick and sudden stops.
note: Impaired drivers often show poor lane control. Weaving between lanes or drifting across lane markings is a classic sign of drunk driving and should be reported. While they may also drive unusually slow or stop suddenly, consistent weaving is a key warning sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is passing prohibited?
options: a:Whenever you are near an intersection.,b:Only when school bus lights are flashing.,c:On a hill or curve where visibility is limited.
note: You must not pass when you cannot see far enough ahead, such as on hills or curves, or in marked no-passing zones. Passing is also prohibited near intersections, railroad crossings, and when a school bus has flashing red lights and is loading or unloading children.
