question: You approach a railroad crossing and hear or see no train; when must you still stop?
options: a:Only if crossing lights are flashing.,b:Never stop if you don't see a train.,c:If a stop sign is posted.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing any time a stop sign is posted, even if you do not see or hear a train. You also must stop when gates are down, red lights are flashing, a flagger directs you to stop, or a train is visible or very close. Never rely only on whether you see a train; always obey the signs and signals at the crossing.

question: Are drivers allowed to pass a school bus when its red lights are flashing?
options: a:False,b:True
note: When a school bus displays flashing red lights, all drivers approaching must stop until the lights are turned off, except on opposite sides of a divided highway with a median.

question: What should drivers do when approaching a flashing yellow traffic light?
options: a:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly,b:Ignore it if no other cars are visible,c:Stop like at a stop sign,d:Slow down and proceed with caution
note: A flashing yellow traffic light means proceed with caution. You should slow down, scan for cross traffic, pedestrians, or other hazards, and be prepared to stop if needed. It does not require a full stop like a stop sign, and you should never speed up to beat the light.

question: What is the most common mistake drivers make while backing?
options: a:Using their horn too much,b:Failing to look both ways behind them,c:Backing too slowly,d:Only relying on rear-view cameras and not mirrors
note: The most common and dangerous mistake when backing is failing to look carefully behind you by turning your head and checking all around, and instead relying mainly on mirrors or a rear‑view camera. Mirrors and cameras do not show the full area behind and to the sides of your vehicle. You should check around the vehicle before getting in, then back slowly while turning your head and looking through the rear window, using mirrors and cameras only as supplements.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. Low beams help you see the road and help others see you without causing glare. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back at you, making it harder to see. Parking lights alone are not bright enough and are not a safe choice while moving.

question: What should you do before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.,b:Honk your horn at least three times.,c:Check your mirrors and blind spots
note: Before passing, you must check your mirrors and blind spots, signal, and make sure the lane is clear. After passing, do not move back too soon; wait until you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.

question: Which is a good practice when driving on major highways?
options: a:Fix cruise control and focus on one distant point,b:Stay alert and be ready to react to hazards,c:Rely on automatic systems without scanning,d:Keep your eyes fixed straight ahead for long periods
note: On major highways, you should stay alert, keep scanning with your eyes, and be ready to react to hazards. Staring at one point or relying only on automatic systems can lead to highway hypnosis and slower reactions.

question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It has no effect on driving skills or judgment.,b:It harms both driving skills and judgment.,c:It helps driving skills but harms your judgment.
note: Alcohol harms both your driving skills and your judgment. It slows reaction time, affects coordination and vision, and makes you more likely to take risks or misjudge situations, even at relatively low blood alcohol levels.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, other road users must allow for what characteristic of large vehicles?
options: a:Their decreased stopping distance,b:Their increased stopping distance,c:Their reduced blind spots,d:Their smaller turning radius
note: Heavy trucks and other large vehicles need more distance to stop because of their size and weight. When driving near them, allow extra space, avoid cutting in front of them, and stay out of their large blind spots.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:The alcohol will help the medicine cure a cold.,b:The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.,c:The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
note: Mixing alcohol with prescription or over‑the‑counter medicines can greatly increase the effects of one or both. This can make you much more drowsy, dizzy, or impaired than using either alone, and it can be very dangerous when driving.

question: To relieve fatigue on a long trip, you should:
options: a:Do occasional arm exercises while driving.,b:Drive with one eye open and one closed.,c:Stop and rest every two hours.
note: On long trips, you should stop at least every two hours to rest, stretch, and refresh yourself. Short breaks outside the vehicle are far more effective and safer than trying to fight fatigue while driving.

question: At a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, when should you proceed after a train passes?
options: a:As soon as the first train passes,b:Only after you have a clear view of all tracks and are sure no other trains are coming,c:Drive around any remaining gates if they appear safe,d:Stop on the first track and watch for another train
note: At crossings with multiple tracks, a second train can come from either direction on another track. After one train passes, wait until gates are fully raised (if present) and you can clearly see down all tracks in both directions before proceeding.

question: If involved in an accident, what should a driver do at the scene?
options: a:Stop near the scene, avoid standing in traffic lanes, and turn off ignitions of wrecked vehicles.,b:Leave the scene if no one appears injured.,c:Stand in traffic lanes to direct drivers around the wreck.
note: If you are involved in a crash, you must stop at or near the scene, help prevent further danger, and check for injuries. Turn off ignitions of wrecked vehicles if it is safe, avoid standing in traffic lanes, and move vehicles out of traffic if they are drivable and there are no serious injuries. You must also exchange information and, when required by law, report the collision to police.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:One driver may continue without stopping.,b:The driver on the left.,c:The driver on the right.
note: At a four-way stop, when two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. Each driver should proceed only when it is their turn and the intersection is clear.

question: What is the best response to a tailgater?
options: a:Change lanes or gradually slow to encourage them to pass.,b:Slam on your brakes to force them back.,c:Speed up to widen the gap.
note: When someone is following too closely, create space rather than reacting aggressively. If possible, change lanes or gradually slow so the tailgater can pass, and maintain a large following distance ahead of you to give yourself more time to react.

question: What is commonly used on some highways to direct drivers into the proper lanes for turning?
options: a:Flashing yellow lights,b:Flashing red lights,c:Arrows painted or displayed for lanes.
note: Arrows painted on the pavement or shown on overhead lane-use signals tell drivers which lanes are for turning and which are for going straight. You must be in a lane marked with a turn arrow if you intend to turn in that direction.

question: You want to back out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. Before moving the vehicle you should:
options: a:Exit the car and walk to the rear to ensure the way is clear.,b:Rev your engine to warn the children.,c:Sound your horn so the children will hear you.
note: When children are nearby, always check behind your vehicle before backing. Walk to the rear and look around the area because small children can be hidden in blind spots that mirrors and cameras may miss. Never rely on revving the engine or honking instead of physically checking.

question: Using a cellphone to talk or text while driving significantly increases your crash risk.
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: Talking or texting on a cellphone while driving takes your attention away from the road. This distraction greatly increases your chance of being involved in a crash, which is why many states restrict or ban phone use while driving.

question: You come to an intersection with a flashing red light. What is the correct action?
options: a:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.,b:Stop at the intersection and wait for a green light.,c:Come to a full stop, then proceed when it is safe.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed only when it is safe. You do not wait for a green light; you treat it as a stop sign-controlled intersection.

question: If a bicyclist disobeys traffic laws, what can happen?
options: a:They can be ticketed,b:They are immune from citations,c:They will always receive only a warning,d:They must be escorted by police
note: Bicyclists generally have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers of motor vehicles. If they disobey traffic laws—such as running stop signs or signals—they can be stopped and ticketed by law enforcement.

question: When is it appropriate to sound your horn?
options: a:To alert others if you have lost control or to warn of immediate danger,b:To express frustration at a slow driver,c:When passing every vehicle in city traffic,d:To greet a friend on the sidewalk
note: Use your horn only to warn others of immediate danger or to help prevent a collision, such as when you lose control or another driver is about to hit you. Do not honk to show anger, hurry other drivers, or greet people, because unnecessary horn use can startle others and create unsafe situations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is driving below the posted speed limit illegal?
options: a:Only when driving in rural areas.,b:When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.,c:When driving so slowly that it disrupts the normal flow of traffic.
note: Driving significantly below the speed of surrounding traffic, without a safety reason, can be illegal because it interferes with the normal flow of traffic and increases the risk of rear-end collisions. If you must drive slowly for safety, move to the right lane or use turnouts where available so faster traffic can pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A good rule to remember about passing is:
options: a:Try to get to the front of slow-moving traffic to see better.,b:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as necessary.,c:Pass on the right whenever possible.
note: A safe passing rule is to drive with the general flow of traffic and pass only when it is truly necessary and legal. Passing should usually be done on the left, with enough clear space and without exceeding the speed limit. Passing on the right is only allowed in specific situations and can be dangerous if done routinely.

question: A driver who is taking a non-prescription drug should:
options: a:Continue to drive regardless of any warning labels.,b:Drink alcohol instead.,c:Read the labels on the drug before driving.
note: Many over-the-counter medicines, such as cold or allergy drugs, can cause drowsiness, blurred vision, or slowed reaction time. Always read the label and warnings before driving, and if you are unsure whether it is safe to drive, ask a pharmacist or doctor for advice.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Stay in the driver's blind spot.,b:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,c:Keep a steady pace.
note: Blind spots are areas alongside and slightly behind a vehicle that the driver cannot see in their mirrors. If you are traveling in another driver’s blind spot, you should either speed up to move ahead safely or slow down to fall back so that you are clearly visible in their mirrors.

question: In vertical traffic lights, what is the order from top to bottom?
options: a:Red on top, yellow in the middle, green on the bottom.,b:Red on bottom, yellow in the middle, green on top.,c:Green on top, red in the middle, yellow on the bottom.,d:Yellow on top, green in the middle, red on the bottom.
note: On a standard vertical traffic signal, the red light is at the top, the yellow (amber) light is in the middle, and the green light is at the bottom. This consistent order helps drivers quickly recognize the signal indication, even from a distance or in poor visibility.

question: Stop lines (solid white lines across lanes) indicate you must stop at:
options: a:Next to churches and schools.,b:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.,c:In curves and on hills.
note: A solid white stop line across your lane shows exactly where you must stop when required, such as at a stop sign, traffic signal, or marked pedestrian crosswalk. You should stop with the front of your vehicle just before the line so pedestrians and cross traffic are protected.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are usually what color and must always be obeyed?
options: a:Green,b:White,c:Blue
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do, such as speed limits, lane use, and parking rules. Most regulatory signs are white with black or red lettering or symbols, and they must always be obeyed because they reflect traffic laws and regulations.

question: If the accelerator gets stuck while you're driving, what is the correct immediate response?
options: a:Shift to neutral, apply steady pressure on the brake, steer to a safe area, then turn off the engine,b:Try to reach under the pedal and pull it up while driving fast,c:Shift to park immediately at highway speed,d:Turn off the ignition while moving in traffic
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep looking at the road, shift the transmission to neutral, and apply steady, firm pressure on the brakes. Steer to a safe place off the road, then once you are stopped, turn off the engine. Do not turn off the ignition or shift to park while moving, as this can cause loss of steering or control.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and keep moving in your lane.,b:Pull to the right curb and stop.,c:Keep driving in your lane.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using flashing lights or a siren, you must immediately pull as close as safely possible to the right side of the road and stop, remaining stopped until the vehicle has passed. This creates a clear path so emergency responders can move quickly and safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The space you need to cross traffic safely depends on which factors?
options: a:Whether you used your turn signal.,b:Road and weather conditions and how quickly traffic is approaching.,c:Presence of a stop sign only.
note: The space you need to cross traffic safely depends on how quickly you and other vehicles can move and stop. Road and weather conditions affect traction and visibility, so you may need a larger gap when the road is wet, icy, or visibility is poor. Heavier or slower vehicles also need more time and space to cross. Turn signals and the mere presence of a stop sign do not determine how much space you need; the key is having a large enough gap in traffic for the conditions.

question: What does a single broken yellow centerline indicate on a two-lane road?
options: a:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is prohibited,b:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is prohibited,c:It marks an emergency lane,d:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is permitted when safe
note: A single broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions. When the line is broken, you may pass another vehicle if it is safe and legal to do so. You must check for oncoming traffic, ensure you have enough distance to complete the pass, and never exceed the speed limit while passing.

question: If another driver is attempting to pass your vehicle, you should:
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Maintain your lane and speed, or slightly reduce speed, to allow a safe pass.,c:Signal to the other driver when it is safe for them to pass.
note: When another driver is passing you, stay in your lane and help them pass safely. Maintain your speed or slightly reduce it so the passing driver can move back into the lane sooner. Do not speed up, and do not signal them when to pass—only they can judge when it is safe. Always check traffic around you so you can react if the passing vehicle has trouble completing the maneuver.

question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:Drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.,b:This type of signal is never used.,c:It has the same meaning as a circular red traffic light — stop and do not turn.
note: A solid red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped for the movement indicated by the arrow. You may not turn in the direction of the arrow while it is red. It has the same meaning as a circular red light for that specific direction: stop before the crosswalk or stop line and wait until a green arrow or green light allows you to proceed.

question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing that has no signals directing traffic?
options: a:Always bring the car to a complete stop.,b:Slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if a train is approaching.,c:All railroad crossings have signals so you will never encounter this situation.
note: At a railroad crossing without lights or gates, you must approach with caution. Slow down, look and listen in both directions for trains, and be prepared to stop if a train is approaching or if you cannot see clearly down the tracks. You are not required to stop every time if no train is coming, but you must always be ready to stop and never proceed onto the tracks unless you are sure they are clear and there is room to cross completely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you enter?
options: a:Either lane at random.,b:The rightmost lane.,c:The lane closest to your previous lane.
note: When turning left onto a one‑way street, you must enter the lane that is nearest to you—the lane closest to the lane you turned from. This keeps traffic organized and prevents you from cutting across multiple lanes, which could cause a collision. Only change lanes after you have completed the turn and it is safe and legal to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and opposing traffic blocks your view, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until you can see all the lanes you must cross before beginning your turn,b:Begin the turn when the first lane clears and accelerate through the rest,c:Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across,d:Lean out and inch forward into the intersection
note: When turning left across multiple lanes of oncoming traffic, you must not start your turn until you can clearly see that every lane you must cross is free of oncoming vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists. Beginning the turn when only the first lane looks clear is dangerous because vehicles in the other lanes may still be approaching at speed.

question: At a school crossing sign you should:
options: a:Always sound your horn when you see children.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always stop
note: A school crossing sign warns you that children may be crossing the road. You must slow down, watch carefully for children, and be prepared to stop if they are in the crosswalk or about to enter it. You are not required to stop every time you see the sign; you stop only when children or a crossing guard are present or traffic laws at that location require it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-lane, two-way road when is it permissible to drive on the left half?
options: a:In a legal passing zone when passing a vehicle traveling in the same direction.,b:When passing in a curve.,c:When passing another vehicle at a railroad crossing.
note: On a two‑lane, two‑way road, you may drive on the left half only when you are passing another vehicle in a clearly marked legal passing zone and only if you can complete the pass safely without interfering with oncoming traffic. You must never drive left of center to pass on a curve or near a railroad crossing because your view and stopping distance are limited.

question: Which is NOT part of stopping distance calculation?
options: a:Braking distance.,b:Reaction distance.,c:Steering ability.
note: Total stopping distance is the distance your vehicle travels from the moment you see a hazard until you come to a complete stop. It is made up of perception distance (seeing the hazard), reaction distance (moving your foot to the brake), and braking distance (while the brakes are slowing the car). Steering ability affects how you avoid hazards but is not a direct part of the stopping distance calculation.

question: Which statement about changing weather and driving is true?
options: a:Be particularly aware of vehicles behind you in bad weather.,b:Only slow down when driving in rain and fog.,c:All of the above.
note: In changing weather, you should always adjust your driving to conditions, which includes slowing down in rain, fog, snow, or ice and increasing following distance. It is especially important to be aware of vehicles behind you, because they may not slow down as early as you do and could need extra space to stop safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, which vehicle has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle on the left has the right-of-way,b:The vehicle approaching from the right has the right-of-way,c:The larger vehicle always has the right-of-the-way,d:The vehicle that honks first has the right-of-way
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no traffic controls.

question: Which of the following can impair your driving?
options: a:Only alcohol,b:Only illegal drugs,c:Only prescription medications,d:Marijuana
note: Marijuana can slow your reaction time, affect judgment, and reduce coordination, all of which make driving unsafe. In reality, many substances can impair driving, including alcohol, illegal drugs, some prescription medications, and even certain over‑the‑counter medicines. Always check how a drug affects you before driving.

question: What do pennant-shaped traffic signs indicate?
options: a:Speed limits.,b:No passing zones.,c:School zones.
note: Pennant-shaped signs are triangular signs pointing to the right and are used specifically to mark the beginning of a no passing zone. When you see this sign, you must not start a pass and must stay in your lane until the zone ends.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is using high beams and doesn't dim them, you should look toward which part of the road?
options: a:Either side,b:The center,c:The right side.
note: When an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams, avoid looking directly at the bright lights. Instead, glance toward the right side of your lane and use the edge line or right side of the road as a guide. This helps protect your night vision while you maintain a safe lane position.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a roundabout you must slow down and yield to which road users?
options: a:Bicyclists and pedestrians in or near the roundabout.,b:Vehicles already in the roundabout.,c:All of the above.
note: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to all traffic already in the circle and to pedestrians and bicyclists who are in or about to enter the crosswalks. Vehicles in the roundabout have the right-of-way, and you must also stop or yield for people crossing at the approaches and exits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit indicates what?
options: a:The speed only commercial vehicles must follow,b:The recommended speed when traffic is heavy,c:The maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions,d:The suggested speed for hazardous conditions
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum (and sometimes minimum) legal speed allowed on that road under ideal conditions. You must reduce your speed below the limit when weather, traffic, or road conditions are less than ideal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Does a double solid yellow line allow passing from either direction?
options: a:True,b:False
note: A double solid yellow line means traffic in both directions is prohibited from crossing the center line to pass. You must stay in your lane and may only cross when making a permitted left turn or when specifically allowed by law, not for passing.

question: How can you avoid making emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Look ahead and maintain a safe following distance.,b:Honk frequently to keep others aware.,c:Drive only in the right lane.
note: Looking well ahead and keeping a safe following distance gives you more time to react to slowing or stopped traffic. This reduces the need for sudden, hard braking and helps prevent rear-end collisions.

question: If you're upset or angry when you get to your car, what should you do?
options: a:Play loud music to distract yourself,b:Take a few minutes to calm down before driving home,c:Drink coffee to become more alert,d:Drive fast to let off steam
note: If you are angry or emotionally upset, you should wait and calm down before driving. Strong emotions reduce your concentration and increase risky behavior, which greatly raises your chances of a crash.

question: A lack of sleep affects driving ability in a way most similar to which of the following?
options: a:The effects of alcohol on driving,b:The effects of amphetamines,c:Feeling angry while driving,d:Taking cold medication
note: Fatigue affects your brain much like alcohol does. When you have been awake for a long time, your reaction time slows, your judgment gets worse, and you may even briefly fall asleep without realizing it. These effects are most similar to driving after drinking alcohol, not to stimulants like amphetamines or just being in a bad mood.

question: What should you do when approaching railroad tracks?
options: a:Look and listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop,b:Speed up to beat the train,c:Drive around lowered gates if no train is sighted,d:Honk and proceed if you think it's safe
note: Railroad crossings must always be approached with caution. Slow down, look and listen carefully for trains in both directions, and be prepared to stop if a train is coming or warning devices are active. Never speed up to beat a train or drive around lowered gates, even if you do not immediately see a train.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before making a turn?
options: a:Flash your headlights before turning,b:Increase your speed to complete the turn,c:Use your turn signal several seconds in advance,d:Turn the wheel sharply then signal
note: Activate your turn signal about three to four seconds before the turn so other road users know your intentions.

question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed slowly and allow it to pass in traffic.,b:Stop immediately in your lane and let it pass if you cannot safely move right.,c:Drive as far to the right as safely possible and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle using lights or siren approaches from any direction, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely move as far to the right side of the road as possible and stop until the vehicle has passed. Do not stop in the middle of your lane if you can move right, and do not try to keep driving alongside or ahead of the emergency vehicle.

question: When driving in fog, you should use your high beam headlights. True or False?
options: a:False,b:True
note: In fog, you should always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams aim light down toward the road and reduce glare, improving your ability to see lane lines and the edge of the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection is blocked by traffic ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.,b:Stay out of the intersection until you can completely pass through.,c:Proceed slowly until the traffic moves.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can drive all the way through without stopping. If traffic ahead is stopped and would force you to stop in the intersection, you must wait behind the stop line or crosswalk. Blocking an intersection can prevent cross traffic and emergency vehicles from moving and is illegal in many jurisdictions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is signaling before turning, changing lanes, or pulling from a curb required?
options: a:It is necessary only if other traffic is present.,b:It is required only during the maneuver,c:It is required by law and is a good driving habit.
note: You must signal at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes; signaling informs other road users of your intentions and is legally required.

question: What are the usual colors for warning signs that indicate hazards ahead?
options: a:Black symbols or letters on a yellow background.,b:White letters on a blue background.,c:Black symbols on a white background.
note: Most general warning signs are yellow with black symbols or lettering. They alert you to curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, and other hazards ahead. In work zones, warning signs are usually orange with black symbols or lettering to highlight construction or maintenance activity.

question: You may drive across a dashed white line when:
options: a:You may drive across a dashed white line at any time.,b:You may drive across a dashed white line only during daylight hours.,c:You may drive across a dashed white line when it is safe to change lanes.
note: A dashed (broken) white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a dashed white line only when it is safe to change lanes—after checking mirrors, blind spots, and ensuring you will not cut off another vehicle. The line does not give you permission to move at any time; safety and proper observation always come first.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:Return to the driving lane when there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,b:Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left.,c:Return to the right side immediately regardless of distance.
note: When passing on a two-lane, two-way road, you should not return to your lane until you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror and there is a safe distance between you. This ensures you do not cut too closely in front of the other driver and that you have enough space to move back without forcing them to brake suddenly.

question: Motorists are required to yield to pedestrians even if the pedestrian is crossing against the traffic signal. True or False?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drivers must always do everything they can to avoid hitting pedestrians, even if the pedestrian is crossing illegally or against the signal. You are still required to yield and slow or stop if needed to prevent a collision.

question: You notice the driver ahead is driving with one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?
options: a:Avoid following the driver's example.,b:Know that the other driver is reducing their safety margin by being inattentive.,c:Give that vehicle extra space.,d:All of the above.
note: When you see a distracted driver, you should not copy their behavior, you should recognize that they are less safe, and you should give them extra space. All of these actions help reduce your risk around an inattentive driver.

question: When there are two railroad tracks, and one train passes, what should you do?
options: a:Assume it's safe once the first train passes.,b:Always stop at the crossing regardless.,c:Look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
note: At a crossing with more than one track, a second train may be coming on another track, sometimes hidden by the first train. After one train passes, stay stopped, look and listen carefully, and only proceed when you are sure no other trains are approaching.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline mean?
options: a:You may pass when safe from either direction.,b:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not permitted.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
note: A double solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means you may not pass from either direction. You may cross it only when turning left safely into or out of a driveway or side road, if not otherwise prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A broken yellow centerline indicates what about the road?
options: a:The road is under repair.,b:You are on a one-way road.,c:You are on a two-way road.
note: Yellow centerlines always separate traffic moving in opposite directions, which means you are on a two‑way road. A broken yellow line also means you may pass another vehicle when it is safe and legal to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive together, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The car on the left proceeds first.,b:The largest vehicle always has priority.,c:The vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This means the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way and may proceed first, while the vehicle on the left must wait.

question: Which factors influence the effects of alcohol on you?
options: a:Amount of food in the stomach, body weight, and time between drinks.,b:The color of the drink.,c:Your level of physical fitness only.
note: Alcohol’s effects depend on several factors, including how much alcohol you drink, your body weight, how much time passes between drinks, and whether you have food in your stomach. Food can slow absorption but does not prevent impairment. Physical fitness does not stop you from becoming intoxicated.

question: If your tire suddenly blows out while driving, what is the recommended immediate action?
options: a:Accelerate to stabilize the vehicle,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly,c:Turn the engine off immediately while moving,d:Slam on the brakes and pull hard to the shoulder
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel to maintain control and keep the vehicle going straight. Do not slam on the brakes. Instead, ease off the accelerator, let the vehicle slow down gradually, signal, and steer smoothly to a safe place off the road.

question: What should be your first reaction to reduced visibility?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Turn on windshield wipers first.,c:Turn on interior lights.
note: When visibility is reduced by fog, rain, darkness, or other conditions, your first response should be to slow down. Reducing speed gives you more time to see hazards and react safely. You may also need to use appropriate lights and wipers, but the immediate safety step is to reduce speed.

question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane mark a crosswalk. Which statement is correct?
options: a:Pedestrians must yield to turning vehicles.,b:No one has right-of-way in a crosswalk.,c:Motor vehicles always have right-of-way in crosswalks.,d:When pedestrians are in crosswalks, drivers must yield and be prepared to stop.
note: Two solid white lines across a lane mark a crosswalk, showing where pedestrians may legally cross. Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked and unmarked crosswalks and be prepared to stop when pedestrians are in or entering the crosswalk. Pedestrians do not have to yield to turning vehicles when they are lawfully in the crosswalk.

question: A steady yellow traffic light means you should:
options: a:Go.,b:Slow down and prepare to stop.,c:Yield to other cars.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and prepare to stop before the intersection. Only continue through if you are so close that stopping safely might cause a rear-end collision or you are already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is a possible maximum speed limit on some rural interstates in Utah?
options: a:65 mph.,b:80 mph.,c:50 mph.
note: Some rural interstate sections in Utah have maximum speed limits up to 80 mph, while others may be posted lower (such as 65, 70, or 75 mph). Always obey the posted speed limit for the specific road and conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, what should drivers do?
options: a:Obey the officer's directions instead of the traffic signal.,b:Follow the directions indicated by the traffic light.,c:Honk at the officer if you disagree.
note: When a law enforcement officer is directing traffic, you must follow the officer’s hand signals and instructions, even if they conflict with traffic lights or signs. The officer’s directions control the intersection until they stop directing traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver's left arm and hand extended downward indicates the driver plans to:
options: a:Stop.,b:Turn left.,c:Turn right.
note: Hand signals are used when turn signals are not visible or not working. A left arm straight out means a left turn, a left arm bent upward means a right turn, and a left arm extended downward with the palm to the rear means the driver intends to slow or stop.

question: Do ramps and bridges freeze before the main road surface?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Bridges, overpasses, and ramps often freeze before the main roadway because cold air circulates above and below them, causing the surface to cool and ice more quickly. Reduce speed and use extra caution on these structures in cold or wet weather.

question: Is it legal and safe to drive under or around a lowered railroad gate?
options: a:Yes — if you are in a hurry,b:Only if directed by another motorist,c:Yes — if you saw the train pass by,d:No — never drive through
note: It is illegal and extremely dangerous to drive through, around, or under lowered railroad gates. A lowered gate means a train is approaching or may still be coming, even if you think it has already passed. You must wait until the gates are fully raised and the warning lights stop before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving much slower than the posted speed and causing traffic to back up on a two-lane road, what should you do?
options: a:Always stay in the left lane to slow traffic,b:Speed up above the limit to keep traffic flowing,c:Pull off the road when safe and let other vehicles pass,d:Refuse to let anyone pass because you have the right-of-way
note: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane road, you must safely pull off the roadway at the first safe place and let other vehicles pass. You should not exceed the speed limit to keep up with traffic, but you also must not unnecessarily obstruct the normal flow of traffic.

question: What is the effect of taking drugs together with alcohol?
options: a:It increases the risk of causing a crash,b:It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone,c:It reduces the effect of alcohol,d:It only affects inexperienced drivers
note: Using alcohol together with any drugs—whether prescription, over‑the‑counter, or illegal—can greatly increase impairment. The combined effects are often stronger than either substance alone, making it much harder to judge distance, react in time, and control the vehicle, which raises the chance of a crash.

question: Which road sections tend to freeze quickly and require extra caution?
options: a:Curvy sections of road.,b:Sections shaded by trees or buildings.,c:Roads in direct sunlight.,d:Bridges and overpasses.
note: Road sections that are shaded by trees, bridges, or buildings often freeze before other areas and stay icy longer because they receive less sunlight. In cold or freezing conditions, be especially cautious on shaded spots, bridges, and overpasses, even if the rest of the road looks clear.

question: Where is parking unlawful?
options: a:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.,b:Anywhere in a parking lot.,c:Always on a hill.,d:In front of a driveway or within an intersection.
note: Parking on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane is unlawful because it blocks pedestrians and cyclists and creates safety hazards. Many other locations are also prohibited, such as in front of driveways, too close to intersections or fire hydrants, or where signs forbid parking. When parallel parking along a curb, you must park close and parallel to the curb, typically within about 12–18 inches, depending on state law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp should:
options: a:Force their way into traffic if necessary.,b:Expect other drivers to yield to them.,c:Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
note: When entering an interstate, you must yield to vehicles already on the highway. Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, signal, and merge only when there is a safe gap. Do not force your way in or expect others to slow or move for you.

question: When must you stop for a school bus?
options: a:Only if the bus is directly in front of you,b:When its red lights are flashing and you are on a two-lane road going either direction,c:Only if children are visible on the road,d:Only when you are behind the bus
note: On a two-lane road with no physical divider, you must stop for a school bus in either direction when its red lights are flashing and the stop arm is extended. Stay stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, even if you do not see children in the road.

question: Compared with daytime driving, night driving is generally:
options: a:No more or less dangerous.,b:More dangerous.,c:Less dangerous.
note: Night driving is more dangerous because you cannot see as far or as clearly, making it harder to spot hazards in time. Glare from headlights, reduced depth perception, and a higher chance of drowsy or impaired drivers all increase crash risk at night.

question: When can a licensed driver under 18 carry non-immediate-family passengers?
options: a:As soon as they receive their license.,b:Only after turning 17.,c:After holding their license for six months.
note: In Utah, most drivers under 18 must wait six months after being licensed before carrying non-immediate-family passengers, unless a specific exception applies (such as driving with a licensed adult). This rule helps new drivers gain experience before managing the distraction of friends in the car.

question: Which behavior helps prevent crashes with other road users?
options: a:Communicating with other road users by signaling and using your horn when appropriate,b:Ignoring other drivers and focusing only on your path,c:Driving only on side streets to avoid traffic,d:Maintaining silence to avoid startling pedestrians
note: Crashes are less likely when other road users can predict what you will do. Use turn signals, brake lights, and your horn when necessary to communicate your intentions so drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians have time to react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Utah, what is the mandatory minimum liability insurance coverage required for all registered motor vehicles?
note: In Utah, the mandatory minimum liability insurance limits are 30/65/25: $30,000 for bodily injury/death of one person, $65,000 for bodily injury/death of two or more people, and $25,000 for property damage.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Utah, you are required to report a motor vehicle crash to the Department of Public Safety (or local law enforcement) if it results in injury, death, or apparent property damage of at least:
note: Utah law requires any driver involved in an accident resulting in injury, death, or total property damage of $2,500 or more to report the accident immediately to law enforcement.
